Customized Shell (or Python API window) can be displayed by checking the checkbox in Home » Window » Python API.

Python commands and execution results are displayed in this area. Black color: PSJ-command information Blue color: Script execution result Red color: Error message Useful tip User can double mouse click on error line information to jump to the specified line in the Customized IDE.

User can run PSJ line by line directly using this Command Line Interface (CLI). Copy ^ Ctrl + C and Paste ^ Ctrl + V operations are supported (for single or multiple lines command) Previous commands can be navigated back and forth using the ↑ Up or ↓ Down key button. User can also double click on a line in the Log window to quickly copy and paste the command to this CLI Auto-fill keywords for Macro, PSJ-Command and PSJ-Utility using ⇥ Tab key. After a keyword is filled, user can use ^ Ctrl + ↑ Up to go backward or ^ Ctrl + ↓ Down to go forward to the near keyword

Repeated operations can make CAE user boring and uncomfortable. The iterative work without automation cannot be completed within a desired duration. Manual operation by human can create mistakes. In depth CAE trainings can be required if modelling is complicated. Each firm has its own design rule/process, design specification/template, etc. thus customized UI specific to each user will be more convenient and helpful.
documents.s: Background problems in daily CAE work

documents.t: To solve the above problems and meet the requirements from our diverged users, PSJ (Python Scripting for Jupiter) is developed, with our 4F moto:

With PSJ, you would have these below features: Jupiter functions in Python script Incorporate with Jupiter’s powerful Pre/Post functions Connect with other software Compatible with Python 3.x and its vast libraries GUI Command Builder: Easy creation of GUI dialog equivalent to Jupiter built-in's Customized IDE: With powerful predicting tips, programming support functions Customized Shell: Error output for debugging More information To know all PSJ solutions, please check out our dedicated sample applications.

This section will introduce Jupiter's customized IDE for PSJ, which can be accessed from the Python ribbon. Currently, this built-in IDE supports: Code highlighter, Auto completion, Tooltip for built in function or user-defined function and Group block of script (Collapse/Expand).

Built-in Python keywords and PSJ API are highlighted in different color for better visualization. The highlighted data is stored in the database folder. In addition, when user double-clicks a word, the same word is highlighted (yellow).

This IDE supports auto-completion. For example, if user types Geometry.Me, a list box will appear and show words that start with Me. The auto-completion data is stored in the database folder and supporting the following: All words in the IDE Python keywords PSJ-Utility PSJ-Command

This IDE supports showing tooltips. For example, if user enters JPT.ClearLog(, a tooltip showing the JPT.ClearLog document is displayed. The docstring from user's defined function is also displayed. The tooltip data is stored in the database folder.
This IDE supports code block grouping (a portion of code can be shown or hidden)

Name Description Shortcut key New Make a new document ^ Ctrl + N Open Open a saved Python script file. (uer can also drag & drop Python file to the IDE window) ^ Ctrl + O Save Save the Python script file ^ Ctrl + S Save As Save the Python script file with another name ^ Ctrl + E Exit Close the IDE ^ Ctrl + Q

Name Description Shortcut key Undo Cancel the executed operation and return to the previous state ^ Ctrl + Z Redo Retry the canceled operation ^ Ctrl + Y Cut Cut the selected text ^ Ctrl + X Copy Copy the selected text ^ Ctrl + C Paste Paste the Cut/Copy text ^ Ctrl + V Import Macro Log Import the macro of the executed command in the form of JPT.Exec(macro command) ^ Ctrl + M Import Python Macro Log Import the executed PSJ-Command ^ Ctrl + J Import Script From Last Run Import the Python script from last run in the IDE ^ Ctrl + L Find Find a specific character in the script. (if user selects some words before executing this function, initial search value will be added with selected words) ^ Ctrl + F Comment Insert the comment tag # before the selected script ^ Ctrl + K Toggle Comment Switch between comment and comment cancellation ^ Ctrl + T Go To Line Go to a specific line in the script ^ Ctrl + G Find And Replace Find and replace the specific characters in the script. (if user selects some words before executing this function, initial search value will be added with selected words) ^ Ctrl + H Convert to Upper Case Convert selected text to upper case ^ Ctrl + ⇧ Shift + U Convert to Lower Case Convert selected text to lower case ^ Ctrl + U Insert Tab Insert a tab to current cursor. In case multiline is selected, tabs will be inserted at the beginning of each line ^ Ctrl + I Duplicate Selection/Line Duplicate selected text. In case selected is empty, current line is duplicated ^ Ctrl + D
Name Description Shortcut key Toggle Text Wrapping Wrap the whole code within the IDE window or let the code stays in one line only ^ Ctrl + W
Name Description Shortcut key Run All Execute all the script F5 Run Selected Execute only the current selected script F6

The IDE database is stored in the Jupiter installation folder/IDEData/. This database can be edited. Content of each file Keywords.dat: Keywords for code highlighter in the IDE PSJCommandCalltips.dat: PSJ-Command auto-completion and tooltip data PSJGuiTooltip.dat: PSJ-GUI auto-completion and tooltip data PSJUtilityCalltips.dat: PSJ-Utility auto-completion and tooltip data PSJPythonHelperCalltips.dat: PSJ Python Helper calltips
PSJ has 3 data types: Python standard built-in type PSJ-Command type PSJ-Utility type PSJ-GUI type Below session will briefly introduce their structures and usages.
Data types used by PSJ-Command functions, including:

There are 2 built-in types: 1. Python Standard built-in type​ The principal built-in types are numerics, sequences, mappings, classes, instances and exceptions. For more information, please visit Python official document 2. This is an instance of a GasketAdditionalBehavior class, represents GasketAdditionalBehavior characteristic of material.

Attribute Description initialGap A Float specifying the initial gap value. Sample Code sample_Mat = Properties.Material.Add(strMaterialName="Sample_Material", listMaterialProperty=[GasketAdditionalBehavior(initialGap=0.2)], iMaterialID=1, iMaterialColor=16131973) JPT.Debugger(sample_Mat) #for checking return value
This is an instance of a Limit Diagram class, represents Limit Diagram characteristic of material.

Attribute Description limitDiagram A List of Tuple specifying all data of Limit Diagram characteristic. temperatureDependency A Boolean specifying the use of temperature-dependent data. dependencies An Integer specifying the number of dependencies in temperature.

Either KEY NAME or ID can be used to define the material property. The ID of material property which was primarily used in functions can be referred to in the Int Notation column. However, in order to explicitly describe meaning of material properties, user can use the KEY NAME instead of specifying ID. For example: PRESSURE_FORCE_LOADING is equal to ID = 63. INT Notation Key Name Description 125 MEAN_STRESS A Tuple specifying the mean stress data. 126 STRESS_AMPLITUDE A Tuple specifying the stress amplitude data. 130 TEMPERATURE A Tuple specifying the temperature-dependent data. Sample Code sample_Mat = Properties.Material.Add(strMaterialName="Sample_Material", listMaterialProperty=[FatigueLimitDiagram(limitDiagram=[ (MEAN_STRESS, [0.8]), (STRESS_AMPLITUDE, [10.0]), (TEMPERATURE, [300.0])], temperatureDependency=True)], iMaterialID=1, iMaterialColor=1415085) JPT.Debugger(sample_Mat) #for checking return value

A Double specifying bias factor, which could be the equal ratio r (if iBiasProgression is 0) or the equal difference (if iBiasProgression is 1). This parameter can only be used only when bEnableMeshCount is True and iBiasMethod is 2 or 3. The default value is 0.0.

An Integer specifying bias method. This parameter is mainly used for local mesh setting on Edge type entity. The number of node to set up is specified in iNodeCount, with bias factor dBiasFactor and progression method iBiasProgression. This parameter and can be one of the following 0: Equal: no bias is set up, nodes are equally distributed. 1: Bias: bias is set up, nodes are distributed so that dense area starts from node with id iBiasNodeId. 2: Bias-sides: bias is set up, nodes are distributed so that dense area starts from both 2 bounding nodes of the edge. 3: Bias-center: bias is set up, nodes are distributed so that dense area is at the middle distance of the edge. This parameter is used only when bEnableMeshCount is True. The default value is 0.

An Integer specifying bias progression method, which can be one of the following: 0: Geometric: distance of nodes will increase by an equal ratio r, where r is bias factor dBiasFactor. For example, when r = 2, if distance between first node and second node is 1, distance between second and third node will be 1 * r = 2, and the next distance will be 4. 1: Arithmetic: distance of nodes will increase by an equal difference d, where d is bias factor dBiasFactor. For example, when d = 2, if distance between first node and second node is 1, distance between second and third node will be 1 + d = 3, and the next distance will be 5. This parameter is used only when bEnableMeshCount is True and iBiasMethod is 2 or 3. The default value is 0.

from pyjdg import * def on_right_click_menu(dlg,name,menu): JPT.ClearLog() #To create an instance of TableCellRangeVector range_vector = TableCellRangeVector() range_vector_2 = TableCellRangeVector() range_1 = TableCellRange(left=1,top=2,right=3,bottom=4) #Methods if menu == "Append": print("Size of TableCellRangeVector before Append():", range_vector.size()) #Size: 0 range_vector.append(range_1) print("Size of TableCellRangeVector after Append():",range_vector.size()) #Size: 1 elif menu == "Extend": range_vector.append(range_1) range_vector_2.append(TableCellRange(left=1,top=3,right=4,bottom=5)) print("Size of TableCellRangeVector before Extend():", range_vector.size()) #Size: 1 range_vector.extend(range_vector_2) print("Size of TableCellRangeVector after Extend():", range_vector.size()) #Size: 2 elif menu == "Clear": range_vector.append(range_1) range_vector_2.append(TableCellRange(left=1,top=3,right=4,bottom=5)) range_vector.extend(range_vector_2) print("Size of TableCellRangeVector before Clear():", range_vector.size()) #Size: 2 range_vector.clear() print("Size of TableCellRangeVector after Clear():", range_vector.size()) #Size: 0 def main(): dlg=JDGCreator(title="Dialog",resizable=True,validation=True) dlg.add_table(name="Table1",rows=10, columns=["Heading1","Heading2","Heading3","Heading4","Heading5","Heading6"], layout="Window",width=700,height=260) dlg.add_hlayout(name="footer",layout="Window") dlg.add_space(orientation="horizontal",layout="footer") dlg.add_button(name="ButtonOk",text="Ok",layout="footer") dlg.add_button(name="ButtonCancel",text="Cancel",layout="footer") dlg.add_space(orientation="horizontal",layout="footer") dlg.add_table_right_menu(name="Table1", menus=["Append","Extend","Clear"]) dlg.generate_window() dlg.on_table_right_menu(name="Table1",callfunc=on_right_click_menu) if __name__=='__main__': main()

An instance of a TableColumnInfo class, represents attributes of a target column inside table.
To create a TableColumnInfo object, defines a variable with TableColumnInfo(...).
A String specifying the name of column. This is a required input.
An Integer A String specifying the data type validation for the column of table. Support 3 types: "String", "Integer" and "Double". This is a required input.
An Integer specifying number of digits after floating point displayed inside a Double column. The default value is 2.
A Boolean specifying the state of filter mode of column of table. True: filter mode will be shown. False: filter mode will be hidden. The default value is False.
A String specifying the name of column.
An Integer specifying the data type validation for the column of table.
An Integer specifying number of digits after floating point displayed inside a Double column. The default value is 2.
An Integer specifying the state of filter mode of column of table. 1: filter mode is using. 0: filter mode is not using. The default value is 0.

Based on the specifying data type of type, all cells of that column accept only that type. If precision is specified to the column which is "String" or "Integer" type, the data type of that column and value of cells will not change. To use filter option, user can set True state to shows filter mode; set False state or ignore this option in script - the both ways will trigger the same action that hides filter mode.

This is an instance of a DPostResultCurve class, represents a Post Result Curve inside Jupiter.

Attribute Description allData The curve data table. The table data is represented by columns and the column titles are in order: frequency, amplitude, phase, real and imagine. The return value is list double vector. id The ID of the curve. The return value is ID (int). rowCount The number of row of the curve data table. The return value is number of row (int). colCount The number of column of the curve data table. The return value is number of column (int). typeID The type ID of response curve. The return value is an int notation of PostResultCurve. curveType The type of response curve . The return value is a string of response curve type (str). frequency The column data of frequency. This attribute is only used for Frequency response. The return value is a double vector of frequency. amplitude The column data of amplitude corresponds to the frequency column. This attribute can be used for both Frequency response and Transient response. The return value is a double vector of amplitude. phase The column data of phase corresponds to the frequency column. This attribute is only used for Frequency response. The return value is a double vector of phase. real The column data of real corresponds to the frequency column. This attribute is only used for Frequency response. The return value is a double vector of real. imagine The column data of imagine corresponds to the frequency column. This attribute is only used for Frequency response. The return value is a double vector of imagine. time The column data of time corresponds to the frequency column. This attribute is only used for Transient response. The return value is a double vector of time.

To develop PSJ, user can use Jupiter built-in IDE, other text editor, or Visual Studio Code from Microsoft (called VSCode for short).

VSCode is an open-source text editor, with the ability to install various extensions to make your Python development faster and easier. Besides all the features of the current Jupiter built-in IDE, VSCode also provides: A debugger An AI co-pilot Linkage to online/local Scripting API document Linting (Hint for fixing the code) caution This is beta version, please do not use for real application. If you have any feedback or question, please contact us.

Install VSCode extension for code highlight, suggestion and snippet via this link Install a Python library for Jupiter-Connection/Debugger using below command (change the link in double quote below if Jupiter was installed in different location): python -m pip install "C:\Program Files\TechnoStar\Jupiter_5.1.0\tools\jupiterutils-4.0.tar.gz" In VSCode, before writing PSJ script, remember to import the installed module using from jupiterutils import *

documents.t: Installation by folder copy (up to V4.0.x) Check the Python version of Jupiter (in V4.0.2 is 3.6.3). Install the same Python version to your machine. Install the module using the pip command in Python to your machine. -> A module folder will be created under the \Lib\site-package folder in the Python installation folder. Copy the created folder under the Jupiter-Pre installation folder \Lib\site-packages. Install with pip (V4.1 or later) Open a command prompt with administrator mode Move to Jupiter installation folder Enter the following command: python -m pip install <module> warning If you update Jupiter, the additional installed libraries will basically remain. However, if the Python version of Jupiter has been updated, the library may stop working. In that case, please reinstall the appropriate version of the library.

PSJ Structure - Understand PSJ basic structure. Scripting API - Read our Scripting API manual (or you can also use our search function at the top right corner). PSJ Extensions - Get to know what PSJ support you writing the script more effectively. External IDE - For writing a complicated script with connection to other software, we recommend user to use Visual Studio Code extension.

IntelliSense is a code-completion aid that includes a number of features: List Members, Parameter Info, Quick Info, and Complete Word. These features help you to learn more about the code you're using, keep track of the parameters you're typing, and add calls to properties and methods with only a few keystrokes. You can use IntelliSense for PSJ modules by setting up environment of VSCode.

Install Python extension for Visual Studio Code. It can installed via Extension Prepare a workspace for your python environment. Create a folder and open it by VSCode. Prepare a file below with name psjsetting, and put it under your python workspace. Modify <user> to your user name. PYTHONPATH=C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\TechnoStar\JPT5.1.0\PythonLib\Lib;C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\TechnoStar\JPT5.1.0\PythonLib\Lib\site-packages;C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\TechnoStar\JPT5.1.0\PythonLib\DLLs; Create .vscode folder under your workspace folder. Place a file below with name settings.json, and put it in there. { "python.envFile": "${workspaceFolder}/psjsetting" } Then the work space will be: Your Folder/ ├── .vscode/ │ └──settings.json ├── psjsetting ├── Test.py Create your script under your folder. Write "import JPT" at top of python file enables to use IntelliSense.

Macro is equivalent to Jupiter built-in dialog function, but without a GUI. For example: CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [10, 10, 10], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_1", 7105764, 0:0) : Make a cube with default input values ImprintLineS([[7.8, 0, 10], [2.2, 10, 10]], [6:26], 1) : Imprint a line on a face between 2 points It is generated right after a dialog function successfully runs. Equivalent to Macro, but PSJ-Command is polished to be compact, easy to write and fully Python compatible. This new PSJ feature is introduced from Jupiter version 5.

PSJ-Command's functions are named after Class-based format and Jupiter’s ribbon. For example, making a cube with default input values: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Part.Cube(dlOrigin=[0, 0, 0], dlLength=[0.01, 0.01, 0.01], ilAxialNodes=[10, 10, 10], strName="Cube_1", iPartColor=7105764, crLocalCoordinate=None) CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [10, 10, 10], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_1", 7105764, 0:0) PSJ-Command's arguments follow our standard naming convention

PSJ-Command's parameters are neglected if the default values are taken. For example, making a cube with default input values: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Part.Cube() CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [10, 10, 10], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_1", 7105764, 0:0)

PSJ-Command is easier to read thanks to its explicit definitions. For example, imprinting a line on a face between 2 points: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Edge.Line(dllPoints=[[0.0078, 0, 0.01], [0.0023, 0.01, 0.01]], crlFaces=[Face(26)]) ImprintLineS([[7.8, 0, 10], [2.2, 10, 10]], [6:26], 1)

PSJ-Command has return value which can make the code looks more Pythonic. For example, deleting 2 cubes just created: PSJ-Command Macro cube1 = Geometry.Part.Cube() cube2 = Geometry.Part.Cube(dlOrigin=[0.01, 0.0, 0.0], strName="Cube_2", iPartColor=6409934) Geometry.DeleteEntity.Part(crlParts=[cube1, cube2]) CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [10, 10, 10], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_1", 7105764, 0:0) CreateCube([10, 0, 0], [10, 10, 10], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_2", 6409934, 0:0) DeletePartCr([3:1, 3:2])

PSJ-Command has error handling built-in which can help developer found the bug faster and easier. For example, inputting a code with a wrong format as below: # Below input has wrong name in the second parameter Geometry.Part.Cube(dlOrigin=[0.01, 0.0, 0.0], strame="Cube_1") After running the above code, the error will be shown in the Python API window: note PSJ interpreter will raise error (exception) when it can not find an entity in database (a database query error). With a wrong input argument (entity ID) then it can lead to a query error rather than return a failed result.
PSJ-Command is fully supported by our customized IDE or VSCode extensions. Read more To get the full list of available PSJ-Command, please refer to the Scripting API.

An Integer specifying the method to separate file. This option allows to separate information into many exported ADX files by the specified type. If iSeparateFile=0, this option would export only 1 ADX file contains all information of all bodies/parts in the model (ModelInfo, Unit, Geometry, LBCs, Process Sequence,...). If iSeparateFile=1, this option would export 2 ADX files, which the first ADX file has same name as analysis Job will contain general information (such as ModelInfo, Unit, LBCs, Job name, Process Sequence, other settings of ADVC Structure analysis). When the last one ADX file which has suffix name "_model", contains Geometry information (such as Node, Part, Element,...). If iSeparateFile=2, this option would export ADX files, which each body/part in model would be written individually Geometry information, Group in model would be written in another file, while other information would be written in the ADX file has same name as analysis Job. If iSeparateFile=3, this option would export ADX file that write information of selected part/body. If selection does not have at least a specific body/part, Jupiter would write all bodies/part (same option as iSeparateFile=0). If iSeparateFile=4, this option would export 1 ADX file contains LBCs information of the chosen LBCs. The default value is 0.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the write group option which output a selected group of faces, elements, nodes as Surface Segment, Element Set and Node set respectively. If True, ADX file would contained group information such as Part, Face, Element(3D,2D,1D), Node,... If False, ADX won't write group information. The default value is False.

A Cursor specifying an existing ADVC job in Assembly Tree to modify it. If this parameter is used, the specified ADVC job will be modified. If it is left None, a new ADVC job will be created. The default value is None.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the Result Reference option is defined or not. If True, this option will allow to active settings of Result Reference. The settings of Result Reference arguments will be valid to use. If False, this option will be disable settings of Result Reference. In this case, the settings of Result Reference arguments will be ignored even though User has set value or not. The default value is False.

An Integer specifying the separate file type. This option allows to separate information into many exported ADX files by selected type. If iSeparateFile=0: None, this option would export only 1 ADX file contains all information of all bodies/parts in the model (ModelInfo, Unit, Geometry, LBCs, Process Sequence,...) If iSeparateFile=1: By Model, this option would export 2 ADX files, which the first ADX file has same name as analysis Job will contain general information (such as ModelInfo, Unit, LBCs, Job name, Process Sequence, other settings of ADVC Structure analysis). When the last one ADX file which has suffix name "_model", contains Geometry information (such as Node, Part, Element,...) If iSeparateFile=2: By Body, this option would export ADX files, which each body/part in model would be written individually Geometry information, Group in model would be written in another file, while other information would be written in the ADX file has same name as analysis Job. If iSeparateFile=3: By Selected Body, this option would export ADX file that write information of selected part/body. If selection does not have at least a specific body/part, Jupiter would write all bodies/part (same option as None). If iSeparateFile=4: By Selected LBCs, this option would export 1 ADX file contains LBCs information of the chosen LBCs. The default value is 0.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the option that export all related Load Boundary Condition. This option could be used when iSeparateFile=3(By Selected Body), if not, this setting is not activated for both True or False. If True, this option would export the ADX file contains related information to LBCs such as Contact, Connection RBE, Bolt Pretension,... If False, this option won't export related information to LBCs such as Contact, Connection RBE, Bolt Pretension,... The default value is False.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the option that use entity name in exported file or not. If True, this option would export the ADX file that write Entity name(Name of the Part/Entity) to Geometry information such as Part, Face,... If False, this option would export the ADX file without writing Entities name to Geometry information. The default value is False.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the option that the Matrix Solver Parameter is defined ot not. If True, this option will allow to active settings of Matrix Solver Parameter. The settings of Matrix Solver Parameter arguments will be valid to use. If False, this option will be disable settings of Matrix Solver Parameter. In this case, the settings of Matrix Solver Parameter arguments will be ignored even though User has set value or not. The default value is False.

An Integer specifying the precondition type. If iPreconditionType=0: Scaling If iPreconditionType=1: CGCG If iPreconditionType=2: CGCG2 If iPreconditionType=3: CGCG2_Diag If iPreconditionType=4: CGCG2-SOR The default value is 0.
An Integer specifying the matrix structure type. If iMatrixStructure=0: Symmetry If iMatrixStructure=1: Asymmetry The default value is 0.
A List of Cursor specifying the list of targets. The target could be Part or LBCs item. The default value is [].

An Integer specifying the load type uses for analysis. If iLoadType=0: Load Case, which is a group of specific Loads, BCs applies on model. The model could apply many Load Cases which may have same setting of LBCs. Exporting ADX file would write all Load Cases. If iLoadType=1: Load, which will export the ADX file stores all Loads, BCs as a 1 Load case only. The default value is 1.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the same output request for all processes. If True, this option would set same output request (Displacement, Stress, Strain,...) for all defined processes. If False, this option would set output request which will base on user's desired result for each process. The default value is True.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the option that would delete floating node or not. If True, this option would export an ADX file without writing floating nodes information. If False, this option would export an ADX file with floating nodes information. The default value is True.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable the option that would separate boundary condition. This option could be used when iSeparateFile=3 (By Selected Body), if not, this setting is not activated for both True or False. If True, this option would export an ADX file would write LBCs information. If False, this option won't export an ADX file would write LBCs information. The default value is True.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable checking whether boundary conditions are duplicated or not. If True, this option checks LBCs duplication when export the ADX file. If False, this option won't check LBCs duplication when export the ADX file. The default value is False.

A Boolean specifying to be enable/disable automatically assign dummy property option. This option used when model that has not assign property yet. If iContactStatus=0, starts from previous subcase. If iContactStatus=1, starts from initial state. The default value is 0.

An Integer specifying how Nastran handles initial gap or penetration of the generated contact elements. This setting is particularly useful if some of your elements unintentionally penetrate each other and you do not wish to modify or rebuild your model. This argument is to be used if iContactType=0. If iInitGapOrPenetration=2, sets the both penetration and gap to zero for all contact elements. The default value is 0.

An Integer specifying whether or not the source region is refined. This argument is to be used if iContactType=0. If iRegionRefine=0, refines the source region based on target surface definition. If iRegionRefine=1, does not refine the source region based on target surface definition. The default value is 0.

A Double specifying the search range. This argument is to be used if iContactType=1. The default value is 0.
A Double specifying the penalty proportional coefficient. This argument is to be used if iContactType=1. The default value is 0.

A Boolean specifying whether to check ID when projecting or not. If True, nodes (on selected meshed faces) will only be projected to CAD faces (in the selected CAD Parts) whose ID is the same as the meshed face of those nodes. For example, if one node is on face 5, that node will only be projected to CAD face (in selected CAD Parts) with the same ID (i.e. 5). If False, ID check will be skipped, and projection takes place when nodes and CAD faces (in the selected CAD parts) are at the closest distance. The default value is False.

A Boolean specifying the status of the process: True: Projected the nodes of the meshed faces to the CAD (Reference) part. False: Cannot project the nodes of the meshed faces to the CAD (Reference) part.

An Integer specifying the number of CPU threads for parallel meshing. This parameter must be smaller than the maximum number of CPU cores. The default value is 0.

A Boolean to enable (True) or disable (False) the preservation of nodes. This parameter is for clean-up step. If disabled, nodes can be moved to improve mesh quality. The default value is True.
A Boolean to enable (True) or disable (False) the correction of internal mesh only. This parameter is for clean-up step. The default value is True.

The plies are numbered starting with 1 for the bottom ply. If the laminate contains an odd number of plies, then model the center ply as half the thickness of the actual center ply. 2: "MEM" - All plies must be specified, but only membrane terms (MID1 on the derived PSHELL entry) are computed. 3: "BEND" - All plies must be specified, but only bending terms (MID2 on the derived PSHELL entry) are computed. 4: "SMEAR" - All plies must be specified, stacking sequence is ignored, MID1=MID2 on the derived PSHELL entry and MID3, MID4 and TS/T and 12I/T**3 terms are set to zero. 5: "SMCORE" - Face plies on one side of the laminate and the core are specified to define a laminate that is symmetric about the midplane of the core. Create a Coordinate System by aligning an Axis direction of Coordinate System follow with an Edge or 2 selected Nodes (1D Element). Besides, it also be used to modify an existing Coordinate System.
A String specifying the name of the Coordinate. The default value is "CRect1".

An Integer specifying the type of Coordinate system, which is one of the following: If iCoordType=0: Rectangular Coordinate - which can be known as Cartesian Coordinate System (Oxyz) If iCoordType=1: Cylindrical Coordinate - (r, φ, z) Coordinate System, where (r, φ, z) are (radial distance, azimuth angle, axial Coordinate or height z) respectively If iCoordType=2: Spherical Coordinate - (r, θ, φ) Coordinate System, where (r, θ, φ) are (radial distance, azimuth angle, polar angle) respectively The default value is 0.

An Integer specifying the Coordinate Axis to align with. This option can be one of the following: If iCoordAxis=0: X axis - Referenced to the X-axis direction, the desired CS will have X axis follow selection direction If iCoordAxis=1: Y axis - Referenced to the Y-axis direction, the desired CS will have Y axis follow selection direction If iCoordAxis=2: Z axis - Referenced to the Z-axis direction, the desired CS will have Z axis follow selection direction The default value is 0.

A Boolean specifying the option to create a new Coordinate or not. This argument uses follow with crEdit, when crEdit is defined, the argument bCreateNew uses to allow creating a new one based on the selected Coordinate System or just modified the selected Coordinate System. If True: A new Coordinate will be created. If False: The Coordinate specified in crEdit will be modified. The default value is True.

A List of Cursor specifying the nodes to determine alignment direction of the Coordinate. This parameter is used only when crEdge is None, otherwise edge option is prioritized. If crEdge is not defined, this argument will be a required input. If this argument is not defined, crEdge must be defined.
A Cursor specifying an edge to determine alignment direction of the Coordinate. If crlNodes is [], this parameter must be defined by a specified edge. This is a required input.

A Cursor specifying an existing Coordinate System to modify. If the bCreateNew is False, this specified Coordinate will be modified, while bCreateNew is True, a new Coordinate will be created. The default value is None.
A Cursor specifying the created Coordinate.

Measure mass by using the specified material's density.
Tools.Measure.Mass.Material(...) Ribbon: Tools » Measure » Mass » Material

A List of Cursor specifying the list of parts to measure the mass. This argurment could be in Part type and/or Bar type. If this parameter is [], crlMassConditions must be specified. If the measurement is applied to crlParts only, then crlParts is a required input. If the measurement is applied to crlMassConditions only, then crlParts would have the default value is [].

A String specifying the material density (default unit: kg/m3). This is a required input.

A String specifying the target value of mass information to be outputted. Depending on the target information, this parameter can be one of the following: If strTarget="Mass": Return the mass value. If strTarget="Gravity Center X": Return the X position of Gravity Center. If strTarget="Gravity Center Y": Return the Y position of Gravity Center. If strTarget="Gravity Center Z": Return the Z position of Gravity Center. If strTarget="Moment Inertial XX": Return the Moment of Inertia about X axis. If strTarget="Moment Inertial XY": Return the product of Moment of Inertia on XY. If strTarget="Moment Inertial YZ": Return the product of Moment of Inertia on YZ. If strTarget="Moment Inertial XZ": Return the product of Moment of Inertia on XZ. If strTarget="Principal Moment X": Return the Moment of Inertia about Principal axis 11. If strTarget="Principal Moment Y": Return the Moment of Inertia about Principal axis 22. If strTarget="Principal Moment Z": Return the Moment of Inertia about Principal axis 33. If strTarget="Traits Vector XX": Return the X direction of Principal axis 11. If strTarget="Traits Vector XY": Return the Y direction of Principal axis 11. If strTarget="Traits Vector XZ": Return the Z direction of Principal axis 11. If strTarget="Traits Vector YX": Return the X direction of Principal axis 22. If strTarget="Traits Vector YY": Return the Y direction of Principal axis 22. If strTarget="Traits Vector YZ": Return the Z direction of Principal axis 22. If strTarget="Traits Vector ZX": Return the X direction of Principal axis 33. If strTarget="Traits Vector ZY": Return the Y direction of Principal axis 33. PSJ-GUI is an UI library supporting user making dialog fast and easily. For example: dlg.add_label(name="Label30",text="Average Size",width=100,text_halign="left",text_valign="top",layout="Layout29") : Add a text label dlg.add_textbox(name="Aver_size",layout="Layout29") : Add a text edit box Different from other Python UI packages (e.g. PyQT, Tkinter, PySide, etc.), PSJ-GUI is fully integrating into Jupiter’s UI framework, help making user’s function same look & feel as Jupiter’s built-in dialog function. PSJ-GUI also supports 2-ways connection, e.g. model picking, table, tab/wizard, etc. Read more To get the full list of available PSJ-GUI, please refer to the Scripting API or get started with our tutorials.

GUI Command Builder is an interactive builder of PSJ-GUI, help making Jupiter dialog or wizard by Drag & Drop operations. User hence does not need to know Python programming language to make UI components in Jupiter. Read more For more information, please read our document about GUI Command Builder.

from pyjdg import * def sampleSelection(dlg): select1=[] select2=[] faces=JPT.GetAllFaces() for f in faces: if f.id % 2 == 0: select1.append(f.id) else: select2.append(f.id) JPT.ClearAllSelection() dlg.activate_selector(selector_id=0) for id in select1: JPT.SelectionByID(JPT.DItemType.FACE, id, True) dlg.activate_selector(selector_id=1) for id in select2: JPT.SelectionByID(JPT.DItemType.FACE, id, True) def main(): dlg=JDGCreator(title="Dialog") dlg.add_face_selector(text="Face 1") dlg.add_face_selector(text="Face 2") dlg.add_label( name="Label2",width=200,height=70, text="Click Apply button and open the selection list and confirm that " "selectors with even IDs are selected in Face 1," "and selectors with odd IDs are selected in Face 2.", text_halign="left",text_valign="top",layout="Window") dlg.generate_window() Geometry.Part.Cube() dlg.on_dlg_apply(callfunc=sampleSelection) if __name__=='__main__': main()

import os import csv import itertools def write_node_data(filename, node_data): headers = [ 'nodenumber', 'x-coordinate', 'y-coordinate', 'z-coordinate', 'temperature', 'heat-transfer-coef' ] with open(filename, 'w', newline='') as f: writer = csv.writer(f) writer.writerow(headers) for node in node_data: writer.writerow(node) def generate_conv_data( size=5, start_pos=-10, step=5, start_temp=-100, temp_step=10, start_coef=0.01, coef_step=0.01 ): positions = [start_pos + i * step for i in range(size)] nodes = [ [i + 1, x, y, z, start_temp + i * temp_step, start_coef + i * coef_step] for i, (x, y, z) in enumerate(itertools.product(positions, repeat=3)) ] return nodes def setup_mapping_view(): JPT.DisableScreenAnimation() JPT.ViewFitToModel() conv_map = JPT.GetEntitiesByID(JPT.EntityType.LBC_MAPPING_THERMAL_CONVECTION, 1)[0] JPT.ShowMappingData(conv_map) def save_mapping_image(image_path): MainWindow.RightClick.ShowHideAllToolbar(iType=1, bShow=False) Home.ToImage(strImgPath=image_path) MainWindow.RightClick.ShowHideAllToolbar(iType=1, bShow=True) def apply_convection_mapping(csv_path): BoundaryConditions.Convection.SurfaceMapping( strName="MappingConvection_1", crlTargets=[Face(24, 26, 22)], iPos=2, iCp=2, iMappedCpIndex0=1, dSearchRange=0.0, iTempUnit=1, strPath=csv_path ) def main(): temp_path = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.TEMP_PATH) csv_path = os.path.join(temp_path, 'node_data.csv') image_path = os.path.join(temp_path, "conv_img.png") #Prepare mapping data (convection) nodes = generate_conv_data() write_node_data(csv_path, nodes) #Preapre Model Geometry.Part.Cube(iPartColor=6409934) apply_convection_mapping(csv_path) #Show mapping result and save image setup_mapping_view() save_mapping_image(image_path) if __name__ == "__main__": main()

PSJ is fully featured with tools and utilities, supports user write Python API script for Jupiter with ease: After Jupiter built-in dialog functions execution, Jupiter will also log out a set of Macro and PSJ-Command to represent the same operations, but in a kind of command language. User can use these commands to rerun the same Jupiter operations. In case user wants to query model's database information (e.g. model's name, IDs, color, etc.), he/she can make use of PSJ-Utility. While writing PSJ, user can take advantage of PSJ Customized Shell and Customized IDE to help debug code easier. The final code can run without a GUI, but if user wants to make it friendlier, PSJ-GUI then can be implemented. Macro PSJ-Command PSJ-Utility PSJ-GUI Customized shell Customized IDE Macro is equivalent to Jupiter built-in dialog function, but without GUI. For example: CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [10, 10, 10], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_1", 7105764, 0:0) : Make a cube with default input values ImprintLineS([[7.8, 0, 10], [2.2, 10, 10]], [6:26], 1) : Imprint a line on a face between 2 points It is generated right after a dialog function successfully runs. Macro can be recorded, run, save and reload using the Macro window. 🡆 Read more about Macro Equivalent to Macro, but PSJ-Command is polished to be compact, easy to write and fully Python compatible. This new PSJ feature is introduced from Jupiter version 5. For example: Macro PSJ-Command CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [10, 10, 10], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_1", 7105764, 0:0) Geometry.Part.Cube() ImprintLineS([[7.8, 0, 10], [2.2, 10, 10]], [6:26], 1) Geometry.Edge.Line(dllPoints=[[0.0078, 0, 0.01], [0.0023, 0.01, 0.01]], crlFaces=[Face(26)]) In detail, PSJ-Command has special features: Functions are named after Class-based format and Jupiter’s ribbon. Parameters are neglected if the default values are taken. Easier to read thanks to its explicit definitions. Has return value which can make the code looks more Pythonic. Has error handling built-in which can help developer found the bug faster and easier. Fully supported by our customized IDE or VSCode extensions. 🡆 Read more about PSJ-Command PSJ-Utility is used for querying model’s information. It is used to complement what is missing from the Macro or PSJ-Command. For example: JPT.Debugger(): Console debugger for PSJ. This utility will show all the related information of the inputted value to the Python API window. JPT.Exec(): Run Jupiter macro JPT.GetAllParts(): Get information of all parts PSJ-Utility is written in the form of: JPT.Function_Name(parameters) 🡆 Read more about PSJ-Utility PSJ-GUI is an UI library supporting user making dialog fast and easily. For example: dlg.add_label(name="Label30",text="Average Size",width=100,text_halign="left",text_valign="top",layout="Layout29") : Add a text label dlg.add_textbox(name="Aver_size",layout="Layout29") : Add a text edit box Different from other Python UI packages (e.g. PyQT, Tkinter, PySide, etc.), PSJ-GUI is fully integrating into Jupiter’s UI framework, help making user’s function same look & feel as Jupiter’s built-in dialog function. PSJ-GUI also supports 2-ways connection, e.g. picking, table, tab/wizard, etc. GUI Command Builder is an interactive builder of PSJ-GUI, help making Jupiter dialog or wizard by Drag & Drop operations. User hence does not need to know Python programming language to make UI components in Jupiter. 🡆 Read more about PSJ-GUI Customized shell is a Jupiter window displays PSJ output and information, with: Python API Window: Python commands and execution results are displayed. Command Line Interface (CLI): user can run Python scripts directly here. Command input is possible by Copy & Paste. 🡆 Read more about Customized Shell To write PSJ easier, we developed a Customized IDE with: Code highlighter Auto completion Tooltip for built in function or user-defined function Group block of script (Collapse/Expand) 🡆 Read more about Customized IDE Built in Python (version 3) compiler PSJ also including useful Python libraries from Python, e.g. pandas, numpy, matplotlib, pptx, scikit-learn, numba, etc. And ability to be integrated to Visual Studio Code using our customized extension.

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to use dlg.add_browser() to select a file and display the selected file's content inside a RichEditCtrl: Create an Open File/Folder and a RichEditCtrl. Display the file's content to the RichEditCtrl after user selects a file.

# Encoding for Japanese # coding: cp932 from pyjdg import * def set_to_rich_text(dlg, path_list): write_to_rich_text = "" for path in path_list: write_to_rich_text += path + "\n" dlg.set_item_text(name='selected_files',text=write_to_rich_text) def main(): dlg=JDGCreator(title="BrowserDemo",resizable=True,validation=True) dlg.add_browser(name="select_files",mode="file",file_filter="All Files(*.*)", multisel=True,layout="Window") dlg.add_richeditbox(name="selected_files",text="",width=200,height=200,layout="Window") dlg.add_label(name="Label3",text="Browser accepts a function that has 2 parameters: " \ "one is dlg and another is a string list, which returns selected files",width=600,layout="Window") dlg.add_hlayout(name="footer",layout="Window") dlg.add_space(orientation="horizontal",layout="footer") dlg.add_button(name="ButtonOk",text="Ok",layout="footer") dlg.add_button(name="ButtonCancel",text="Cancel",layout="footer") dlg.add_space(orientation="horizontal",layout="footer") dlg.generate_window() dlg.on_browse(name="select_files",callfunc=set_to_rich_text) if __name__=='__main__': main()

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to capture model image without screen effect: Take a screenshot of the current viewed model and output to a *.jpg file. Disable screen update, screen animation and message output to Macro/Python API window to improve PSJ performance. Notice Avoid using JPT.Disable... functions in a loop. Once disabled, it will affect until it is enabled again.

# Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() import time import os start = time.time() # Turn off output message to Macro and Python API windows # It will be automatically enabled again after PSJ finishes running JPT.DisableOutputMessage() # Disable screen animation (It is necessary when you capture model on the Visualization window) # It will be automatically enabled again after PSJ finishes running JPT.DisableScreenAnimation() # Prepare a cube Geometry.Part.Cube() # Capture model image and output it to your local folder JPT.ViewFitToModel() strDesktopPath = os.path.join(os.path.join(os.environ['USERPROFILE']), 'Desktop') strImagePath = strDesktopPath + "/cube_image.jpg" Home.ToImage(strImgPath=strImagePath) # Collapse assembly tree window to avoid GUI update JPT.CollapseAssemblyTree() # Start transaction point JPT.BeginDatabaseTransaction("Change element color operation") # Change color of all elements for elem in JPT.GetAllElems(): elem.color = JPT.GetRandomJPTColor() # End transaction point JPT.EndDatabaseTransaction() # Capture the current model image and output it to your local folder strNewImagePath = strDesktopPath + "/cube_new_image.jpg" Home.ToImage(strImgPath=strNewImagePath) # Enable screen animation JPT.EnableScreenAnimation() # Turn on output message to Macro and Python API windows JPT.EnableOutputMessage() # Get the execution time elapsed_time = time.time() - start print('Time Total: ' + str(elapsed_time) +'s')

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to compare content of two files (log files, output files, etc.): Get path of installed Jupiter. Set the path of two files which their content will be compared. Compare content of two files. Then display the comparison result (same or different) in Python API window.

# Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Import file compare module 'filecmp' import filecmp # Get path of installed Jupiter jupiterPath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.PROGRAM_PATH) # Set the path of two files which their content will be compared. myPath = jupiterPath + '/SampleData/PSJ/PSJ-Utility/Utils' file1 = myPath + '/FileCompare1.txt' file2 = myPath + '/FileCompare2.txt' # Compare content of two files. Display the comparison information at Python API window. is_same_file = filecmp.cmp(file1,file2) if is_same_file == 0: print('Content of two files is different') else: print('Content of two files is same')

# Encoding for Japanese # coding: cp932 from pyjdg import * def on_menu(dlg,name,menu): cellvector=dlg.get_table_sel_cell(name) if menu=="Set Column Width using Dialog": dlg.set_table_column_width(name="Table1", col=cellvector[0].col_number) if menu=="Set Column Width equal 400": dlg.set_table_column_width(name="Table1", col=cellvector[0].col_number,width=400) elif menu=="Get Column Width": col_width = dlg.get_table_column_width(name="Table1", col=cellvector[0].col_number) print("Column "+str(cellvector[0].col_number)+ " width is: "+str(col_width)) def main(): dlg=JDGCreator(title="Dialog",resizable=True,validation=True) dlg.add_table(name="Table1",rows=5, columns=["Heading1","Heading2"], layout="Window",width=260,height=260) dlg.add_hlayout(name="footer",layout="Window") dlg.add_space(orientation="horizontal",layout="footer") dlg.add_button(name="ButtonOk",text="Ok",layout="footer") dlg.add_button(name="ButtonCancel",text="Cancel",layout="footer") dlg.add_space(orientation="horizontal",layout="footer") dlg.add_table_right_menu(name="Table1", menus=["Set Column Width using Dialog", "Set Column Width equal 400","Get Column Width"]) dlg.generate_window() dlg.on_table_right_menu(name="Table1",callfunc=on_menu) if __name__=='__main__': main()

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to convert betweens object types (Base <--> Child): Get list of all parts in current model. Check information of DBody object. Convert DBody object to DItem entity object (base class) which contains more information. Convert DItem entity object (base class) back to DBody object. Base class: Entity Child class: Body, Face, Edge, Group, Node, Elem, etc. In this tutorial, Body object is used, but other objects can be used as the same way.

# Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Create a cube Geometry.Part.Cube(strName="Cube_1") # Fit view of model on display view JPT.ViewFitToModel() # Get list of all parts in current model # This function returns list of parts (Body). Object type: DBody # Check information of DBody object listParts = JPT.GetAllParts() cubePart = listParts[0] JPT.Debugger(cubePart) # Convert DBody object to DItem entity object (base class) # Check information of DItem entity object cubeDItem = JPT.CastToDItem(cubePart) JPT.Debugger(cubeDItem) # Convert back DItem entity object (base class) to DBody object # Check information of DBody object new_cubePart = JPT.CastDItemToDBody(cubeDItem) JPT.Debugger(new_cubePart)

This tutorial demonstrates how to make a custom bolt by using a pre-defined template of PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro. It will also integrate the PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro to a customized UI dialog by using GUI Command Builder. In this tutorial, you’ll learn How to get and make use of the PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro. Implement the PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro to a general Python script for the automation process. Creat a dialog by using GUI Command Builder. Integrate the user script in (2.) to the created dialog in (3.) to make a custom UI function. Add the created custom UI function in (4.) to Jupiter's ribbon and use it.

About this dialog: you will make an UI dialog to integrate the customized PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro for the automation process. After selecting the bolt's size and pressing Apply or OK button (left picture), a user-standard bolt will be created and shown in Jupiter's screen (right picture). In general, below are the steps that you will follow: Get PSJ-Command or Macro: Execute the available functions in Jupiter to get the respective PSJ-Command or Macro. Create DEF function in Python: Combine PSJ-Command or Macro with Python based script in order to create an user-defined function fully. Create User Interface (UI): Use GUI Command Builder to make an UI dialog connecting to the user-defined function in (2.). Implement: Register the created UI dialog in (3.) to Jupiter.

In this section, you can learn how to get the PSJ-Command/Macro from the executed function. Within this example, you also can know how to implement the PSJ-Command/Macro of the following functions: Geometry » Create Entity » Part » Cylinder function. Assemble » Assemble » Assemble Faces function. Geometry » Edit Entity » Merge Entities » Parts function. Rename the part on the Assembly window.

Use Geometry » Create Entity » Part » Cylinder function to make 2 cylinders in sequence: one for bolt head, the other for bolt body. ※1. The number of the edge of the bolt head. In this case, we inputted 6 for 6 edges of the bolt head. You can change it by your own. ※2. Value of L parameter will be equal to (Height - Origin-Y), and Origin-Y will be equal to the height of bolt head - 0.005. The reason is to prevent zero-touch case. Then, you can see the created bolt on the Jupiter's display window: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Part.Cylinder(strName="Bolt_Head", dTopOuterRadius=0.003005, dBottomOuterRadius=0.003005, dHeight=0.002, iCircularNodes=6) Geometry.Part.Cylinder(strName="Bolt_Body", dlOrigin=[0.0, 0.001995, 0.0], dTopOuterRadius=0.0015, dBottomOuterRadius=0.0015, dHeight=0.010005, iPartColor=6409934) CreateCylinderPart("Bolt_Head", 0:0, 0, 0, [0, 0, 0], 0.001, 0.003005, 0.001, 0.003005, 0.002, 6, 10, 7105764) CreateCylinderPart("Bolt_Body", 0:0, 0, 0, [0, 0.001995, 0], 0.001, 0.0015, 0.001, 0.0015, 0.010005, 36, 10, 6409934)

Then, use Assemble » Assemble » Assemble Faces function to generate share faces between the created 2 cylinders: Input tolerance = 0.01 to the Tolerance textbox. Click on the Find button to find all the faces between the created 2 cylinders. Click on the Apply or OK button to generate share faces finding from (2.). A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Assemble.FindMatingFaceEx(crlTaBodies=[Part(1, 2)], dMatingTol=1e-05) Assemble.AssembleFaceEx(ilPairFaceToMakeShareFace=[9, 3], dTolerance=1e-05, iTypeConnectPos=0) AssembleFaceMatingStep([], [], [3:1, 3:2], 1e-05) AssembleFaceEx([9, 3], 1e-05, 0, 0)

Next, use Geometry » Edit Entity » Merge Entities » Parts function to merge 2 cylinders into 1 part. This part will be considered as a simple bolt geometry using in this tutorial: Select 2 created cylinders with their shared faces. Click on the Apply or OK button to merge them into 1 part. A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.MergeEntities.Parts(crlParts=[Part(1, 2)], dMergeTolerance=1e-05) MergePart(1e-08, 1, [3:1, 3:2])

Finally, right-click on the merged part in the Assembly window to rename this part to BOLT. A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Assembly.RightClick.Rename(strNewName="BOLT", crItem=Part(1)) RenameItem("BOLT", 3:1)

To recap, below is the total PSJ-Command and Macro collected in the above steps: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Part.Cylinder(strName="Bolt_Head", dTopOuterRadius=0.003005, dBottomOuterRadius=0.003005, dHeight=0.002, iCircularNodes=6) Geometry.Part.Cylinder(strName="Bolt_Body", dlOrigin=[0.0, 0.001995, 0.0], dTopOuterRadius=0.0015, dBottomOuterRadius=0.0015, dHeight=0.010005, iPartColor=6409934) Assemble.FindMatingFaceEx(crlTaBodies=[Part(1, 2)], dMatingTol=1e-05) Assemble.AssembleFaceEx(ilPairFaceToMakeShareFace=[9, 3], dTolerance=1e-05, iTypeConnectPos=0) Geometry.MergeEntities.Parts(crlParts=[Part(1, 2)], dMergeTolerance=1e-05) Assembly.RightClick.Rename(strNewName="BOLT", crItem=Part(1)) CreateCylinderPart("Bolt_Head", 0:0, 0, 0, [0, 0, 0], 0.001, 0.003005, 0.001, 0.003005, 0.002, 6, 10, 7105764) CreateCylinderPart("Bolt_Body", 0:0, 0, 0, [0, 0.001995, 0], 0.001, 0.0015, 0.001, 0.0015, 0.010005, 36, 10, 6409934) AssembleFaceMatingStep([], [], [3:1, 3:2], 1e-05) AssembleFaceEx([9, 3], 1e-05, 0, 0) MergePart(1e-08, 1, [3:1, 3:2]) RenameItem("BOLT", 3:1) Use the above scripts, now parameterize the numbers and add some built-in Python functions (if…else, for, while, etc.) to make the script adapt to different input parameters. To execute the code in Python, use 2 ways as below: PSJ-Command: Copy and paste directly to the creating Python code. Macro: use the following structure to execute the code in pythonJPT.Exec(“Macro”). info The PSJ-Command and/or Macro is added to create the bolt according to the value generated by user. From now, user can combine the knowledge about Python language and the just generated Macro to create def function. The following process will show you the way to prepare important def of this example:

import re from os import listdir from os.path import isfile, join from pyjdg import * import random In which: re is a library helping you to modify string. listdir, isfile, join are the libraries helping you to get all files inside a specific folder. pyjdg is a library to enable GUI Command Builder. random is a library to get a random number (for setting part's color).

The output structure of the parameters of bolt size will follow the following structure: [Bolt head's height, Bolt head's diameter, Bolt body's diameter]. def get_bolt_size(get_param_bolt_type): ''' Bolt type for standard size''' if get_param_bolt_type == 0: # M3 return [2e-3, 6.01e-3, 3e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 1: # M4 return [2.8e-3, 7.66e-3, 4e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 2: # M5 return [3.5e-3, 8.79e-3, 5e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 3: # M6 return [4e-3, 11.5e-3, 6e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 4: # M8 return [5.3e-3, 14.38e-3, 8e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 5: # M10 return [6.4e-3, 18.9e-3, 10e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 6: # M12 return [7.5e-3, 21.1e-3, 12e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 7: # M14 return [8.8e-3, 24.49e-3, 14e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 8: # M16 return [10e-3, 26.75e-3, 16e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 9: # M18 return [11.5e-3, 30.14e-3, 18e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 10: # M20 return [12.5e-3, 33.53e-3, 20e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 11: # M22 return [14e-3, 35.72e-3, 22e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 12: # M24 return [15e-3, 39.98e-3, 24e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 13: # M27 return [17e-3, 45.2e-3, 27e-3] elif get_param_bolt_type == 14: # M30 return [18.7e-3, 50.85e-3, 30e-3] else: print("error") tip The given values are the reference values. You can change those values based on your standard.

Create the below def function for executing whenever changing the bolt type (Update preview pictures). def change_bolt_pic(dlg): ''' Change the picture of the select bolt ''' picture_folder = re.sub(re.escape("\\"), "/", (JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.PROGRAM_PATH) + r'SampleData\PSJ\PSJ-GUI\CreateBolt\CreatingBolt_Pics')) only_file = [f for f in listdir(picture_folder) if isfile(join(picture_folder, f))] for i in only_file: file_name, file_extension = i.split('.') if dlg.get_item_text('bolt_type') == file_name: full_path = picture_folder + "/" + i dlg.set_image_file('ImageCtrl', full_path) In which: picture_folder is a parameter to get full path to the stored preview pictures. We stored all the related files relating to this tutorial in the Jupiter installation folder. picture_folder is the parameter refering to the stored location to get stored pictures. The stored localtion: Jupiter installation folder » SampleData » PSJ » PSJ-GUI » CreateBolt » CreatingBolt_Pics

documents.t: With the current output value of the Assemble Faces function, we need to modify before using it. The current output of the finding pair faces option will have the following structure (For example): 1, ["72-47"]. Or, you can understand via the following structure: 1, ["face1-face2","face3-face4","face5-face6",...] So, to make it can be used, you can use the following def function (or you can create your own function). tip Whenever start using a function, you should check it's output values and type. In Jupiter, we're supporting a utility called JPT.Debugger()Console debugger for PSJ. This utility will show all the related information of the inputted value to the Python API window. def replace_str(err, in_str): mod_str = in_str for i in range (len(err)): mod_str = mod_str.replace(str(err[i]), " ") mod_str = re.sub("s+", " ", mod_str).strip().split(" ") return mod_str

documents.t: Based on the created PSJ-Command and Jupiter's Macro from the previous steps, the on_execute_button_clicked() function is responsible for implementing the Apply or OK button. It will have the following structure: PSJ-Command Macro def on_execute_button_clicked(dlg): ''' Create a bolt when click on the Apply or OK button. Parameters: dlg: Call class dlg for using [dlg.] - API between the GUI Command Builder and Python. Results: A bolt is created when Apply or OK button is clicked. ''' # Preparing parameters for the creation part_name = dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name") coord_system = int(dlg.get_combobox_sel(name="coord_system")) bolt_type = int(dlg.get_combobox_sel(name="bolt_type")) [k, e, d] = get_bolt_size(bolt_type) # Get size of the creating bolt based on the selected bolt_type option nut_radius = e/2 thread_radius = d/2 cylinder_height = k cylinder_position = cylinder_height bolt_length = dlg.get_item_text(name="bolt_length") get_param_bolt_length = float(bolt_length)*0.001 color = random.randint(10000, 60000000) # Creating bolt head and bolt body Geometry.Part.Cylinder(strName=part_name, dlOrigin=[0, 0, 0], dTopOuterRadius=nut_radius, dBottomOuterRadius=nut_radius, dHeight=cylinder_height, iCircularNodes=6, iPartColor=color) Geometry.Part.Cylinder(strName=part_name, dlOrigin=[0, cylinder_position, 0], dTopOuterRadius=thread_radius, dBottomOuterRadius=thread_radius, dHeight=get_param_bolt_length, iPartColor=color, crLocalCoordinate=Coord(coord_system)) # Making assemble faces all_part = sorted([a.id for a in JPT.GetAllParts()], reverse = False) assemble_face_func = JPT.Exec('AssembleFaceMatingStep([], [], [3:{0}, 3:{1}], 0.0003).' .format(all_part[-2], all_part[-1])) errstr = ", []-\"" JPT.Exec('AssembleFaceEx([{0}, {1}], 0.0003, 0, 0)' .format(replace_str(errstr, assemble_face_func)[-2], replace_str(errstr, assemble_face_func)[-1])) # Merging 2 created parts into 1 part JPT.Exec('MergePart(1e-05, 1, [3:{0}, 3:{1}])'.format(all_part[-2], all_part[-1])) # Show the created part JPT.Exec('View Fit To Model()') # Change the part_name parameter (On the GUI) automatically if str(dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name")).find("_") != -1: if dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name").split("_")[-1].isdigit() == True: new_name = dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name")[:-(len(dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name") .split("_")[-1]) + 1)] + "_" + str(int(dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name").split("_")[-1]) + 1) else: new_name = dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name") + "_" + str(len([_.id for _ in JPT.GetAllParts()]) + 1) else: new_name = dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name") + "_" + str(len([_.id for _ in JPT.GetAllParts()]) + 1) dlg.set_item_text(name="part_name", text=new_name) def on_execute_button_clicked(dlg): ''' Creating a bolt when click on the Apply or OK button Parameters: dlg: Call class dlg for using [dlg.] - API between the GUI Command Builder and Python. Results: A bolt is created when Apply or OK button is clicked. ''' # Preparing parameters for the creation part_name = dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name") coord_system = int(dlg.get_combobox_sel(name="coord_system")) bolt_type = int(dlg.get_combobox_sel(name="bolt_type")) [k, e, d] = get_bolt_size(bolt_type) # Get size of the creating bolt based on the selected bolt_type option nut_radius = e/2 thread_radius = d/2 cylinder_height = k cylinder_position = cylinder_height bolt_length = dlg.get_item_text(name="bolt_length") get_param_bolt_length = float(bolt_length)*0.001 color = random.randint(10000, 60000000) # Creating bolt head and bolt body JPT.Exec('CreateCylinderPart("{0}", 27:{1}, 0, 0, [0, 0, 0], 0.001, {2}, 0.001, {2}, {3}, 6, 10, {4})' .format(part_name, coord_system, nut_radius, cylinder_height, color)) JPT.Exec('CreateCylinderPart("{0}", 27:{1}, 0, 0, [0, {2}, 0], 0.001, {3}, 0.001, {3}, {4}, 36, 10, {5})' .format(part_name, coord_system, cylinder_position, thread_radius, get_param_bolt_length, color)) # Making assemble faces errstr = ", []-\"" all_part = sorted([a.id for a in JPT.GetAllParts()], reverse = False) assemble_faces = JPT.Exec('AssembleFaceMatingStep([], [], [3:{0}, 3:{1}], 0.0003).' .format(all_part[-2], all_part[-1])) JPT.Exec('AssembleFaceEx([{0}, {1}], 0.0003, 0, 0)' .format(replace_str(errstr, assemble_faces)[-2], replace_str(errstr, assemble_faces)[-1])) # Merging 2 created parts into 1 part JPT.Exec('MergePart(1e-08, 1, [3:{0}, 3:{1}])'.format(all_part[-2], all_part[-1])) # Show the created part only JPT.InverseHideBodies(all_part[-2]) JPT.ViewFitToModel() # Change the part_name parameter (On the GUI) automatically if str(dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name")).find("_") != -1: if dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name").split("_")[-1].isdigit() == True: new_name = dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name")[:-(len(dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name") .split("_")[-1]) + 1)] + "_" + str(int(dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name").split("_")[-1]) + 1) else: new_name = dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name") + "_" + str(len([_.id for _ in JPT.GetAllParts()]) + 1) else: new_name = dlg.get_item_text(name="part_name") + "_" + str(len([_.id for _ in JPT.GetAllParts()]) + 1) dlg.set_item_text(name="part_name", text=new_name)

To create a dialog with title and execution buttons, please do the following steps: In the opened dialog, click on the Dialog component inside the Hierarchy window. After clicking on the Dialog component (1.), change its properties as the below suggestions: 2.1. Title: Bolt Creation. 2.2. Validation: Checked on (Enable this option). 2.3. Apply Button: Checked on (Enable this option). 2.4. Ok Button: Checked on (Enable this option). 2.5. Cancel Button: Checked on (Enable this option).
documents.s: 3.2. Create a dialog with title and execution buttons

documents.t: To add the required components to the creating dialog, please follow the following steps: Add Unit System: mm by using Label component. Add an image as a preview picture into the creating dialog by using ImageCtrl component. Add Part Name textbox to input the name of the creating bolt by using Layout, Label and TextBox components. Add Coordinate System selection to select the reference coordinate system for creating bolt by using Layout, Label and ComboBox components. Add Bolt Type selection to select the reference coordinate system for creating bolt by using Layout, Label and ComboBox components. Add Update preview bolt size button to update the preview bolt picture on the GUI based on the selected bolt type by using Layout and Button components. Add Bolt Length textbox to input the length of the creating bolt by using Layout, Label and TextBox components.

After creating your own UI, you need to export it to Python file (*.py): Click on the Show or hide code window(F1) button to show/hide the UI code (Python format). Click on the Export PSJ button to export the created UI to Python file (*.py).

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to convert unit between user GUI and PSJ-Command/macro: Use JPT.ConvertFromDocUnit() to convert the inputted value from the current Jupiter unit system to SI[m] unit (Jupiter macro unit)). Use JPT.ConvertFromMacroUnit() to convert the inputted value from the specified unit to the SI[m] unit (Jupiter macro unit). Use JPT.ConvertValueToDocUnit() to convert the inputted value from SI[m] units (Jupiter macro units) to the current Jupiter unit system. Use JPT.ConvertValueToMacroUnit() to convert the inputted value from the SI[m] unit (Jupiter macro unit) to the specified unit.

# Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Set input value inputValue = 1 # Convert input value from the current Jupiter unit to Jupiter macro unit (SI[m] unit) # To check current Jupiter unit, refer Home -> Preferences -> Unit -> Current Unit frDoc_toMacro = JPT.ConvertFromDocUnit(inputValue, JPT.UnitType.Unit_Length) print("From current Jupiter unit system: {} -> To Jupiter macro unit (SI[m]): {}" .format(inputValue, frDoc_toMacro)) # Convert input value from the specified unit to Jupiter macro unit (SI[m] unit) frSpeci_toMacro = JPT.ConvertFromMacroUnit(inputValue, JPT.UnitType.Unit_Length, "mm") print("From specified unit 'mm': {} -> To Jupiter macro unit (SI[m]): {}" .format(inputValue, frSpeci_toMacro)) # Convert input value from Jupiter macro unit (SI[m] unit) to the current Jupiter unit frMacro_toDoc = JPT.ConvertValueToDocUnit(inputValue, JPT.UnitType.Unit_Length) print("From Jupiter macro unit (SI[m]): {} -> To current Jupiter unit: {}" .format(inputValue, frMacro_toDoc)) # Convert input value from Jupiter macro unit (SI[m] unit) to the specified unit 'mm' frMacro_toSpeci = JPT.ConvertValueToMacroUnit(inputValue, JPT.UnitType.Unit_Length, "mm") print("From Jupiter macro unit (SI[m]): {} -> To specified unit 'mm': {}" .format(inputValue, frMacro_toSpeci))

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to create a group of elements by using a CSV template file: Read content from csv file (contains element IDs) line by line. Create a group of elements from the csv file. Please prepare the text csv file with ID of elements in local disk to use the code in sample.

# Import 'exists' from module 'os.path' import os # Import 'csv' import csv # Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Prepare a cube JPT.Exec('CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [0.01, 0.01, 0.01], [10, 10, 10], "Cube_1", 12999622, 0:0)') # Declare path name of csv file listElems = [] strJupiterPath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.PROGRAM_PATH) fileCSV = strJupiterPath + '/SampleData/PSJ/PSJ-Utility/Utils/ElementID.csv' # Read content from csv file (contains element IDs) line by line if os.path.exists(fileCSV): with open(fileCSV) as csv_file: csv_reader = csv.reader(csv_file, delimiter=',') for row in csv_reader: elemID = row[0] listElems.append(Elem((elemID))) else: print("File does not exist!") # Create a group of elements from the csv file Tools.Group.CreateGroup(strGroupName="Group_Element", crlTargets=listElems)

This tutorial demonstrates how to create a model and setting boundary conditions for plan stress problem by using a pre-defined template of PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro. After that, using TS-SunShine to solve the plane stress problem exporting from Jupiter. It will also integrates the PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro to a customized UI dialog by using GUI Command Builder. In this tutorial, you’ll learn How to get and make use of the PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro. Implement the PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro to a general Python script for the automation process. Call TS-SunShine to solve the exported file from Jupiter. Open powerpoint and put the outputted values to powerpoint to create a report. Creat a dialog by using GUI Command Builder. Integrate the user script in (2.) to the created dialog in (3.) to make a custom UI function. Add the created custom UI function in (4.) to Jupiter's ribbon and use it.

About this dialog: you will make an UI dialog to integrate the customized PSJ-Command/Jupiter's Macro for the automation process. After inputting values and clicking on the Apply/OK button, user can get the report containing the result of the created model. In general, below are the steps that you will follow: Get PSJ-Command or Macro: Executing available functions in Jupiter to get the respective PSJ-Command or Macro. Create DEF function in Python: Combining PSJ-Command or Macro with Python based script in order to create a full user function. Create User Interface (UI): Using GUI Command Builder to make an UI dialog connecting to the user function in (2.). Implement: Registering the created UI dialog in (3.) to Jupiter.

In this section, you can learn how to get the PSJ-Command/Macro from the executed function. Within this example, you also can know how to implement the PSJ-Command/Macro of the following functions: Geometry » Create Entity » Part » Cube function. Geometry » Create Entity » Part » Cylinder function. Assemble » Combination » Boolean function. Geometry » Delete Entity » Face function. Meshing » Surface Meshing function. Properties » Material function. Properties » Shell function. Boundary Conditions » Constraints » Fixed Constraints function. Boundary Conditions » Force » General function. Analysis » TSSS function. Undo command by using Ctrl + Z Renaming part on the Assembly window.

Using Geometry » Create Entity » Part » Cube function to make a cube using as the base model of the plane stress model. Then, you can see the created cube on the Jupiter's display window: The process will be shown as below: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Part.Cube(dlLength=[0.02, 0.001, 0.015], strName="planestress_model1", iPartColor=7531634) CreateCube([0, 0, 0], [0.02, 0.001, 0.015], [10, 10, 10], "planestress_model1", 7531634, 0:0)

Using Geometry » Create Entity » Part » Cylinder function to make a cylinder for making a hole in the center of the plan stress model. Then, you can see the created cylinder and the created cube on 1.1. on the Jupiter's display window: The process will be shown as below: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.Part.Cylinder(dlOrigin=[0.01, -0.001, 0.0075], dTopRadius=0.001, dBottomRadius=0.001, dHeight=0.003, iPartColor=7697908) CreateCylinderFrustum([0.01, -0.001, 0.0075], 0.001, 0.001, 0.003, 36, 10, "Cylinder_1", 7697908, 0:0)

Using Assemble » Combination » Boolean function and select Subtract option to make a hole in the center of the plane stress model. This function will use the created cylinder (Step 1.1.) and the created cube (Step 1.2.). After using this function, the creating model will be the same as below: The process will be shown as below: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Assemble.BooleanEx([Part(1, 2)], strNameSuffix="", iBooleanType=1) BooleanEx([3:1, 3:2], "", 1, 0, 0, 0)

documents.t: On the Assembly window, Right Click on the subtracted part and select Rename option to change the name of the part after subtracting. Then, you can see the new name of the subtracted part: The process will be shown as below: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Assembly.RightClick.Rename(strNewName="planstress_model1", crItem=Part(1)) RenameItem("planstress_model1", 3:1)

Using Geometry » Delete Entity » Delete Entity » Face function to create plane stress model by deleting all the unnecessary faces. Then, you can see the model after deleling faces: The process will be shown as below: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Geometry.DeleteEntity.Face([Face(31, 22, 25, 23, 26, 24)]) DeleteFaceCr([6:31, 6:22, 6:25, 6:23, 6:26, 6:24], 1)

tip Before executing Surface Meshing function, you should enable Show mesh line option. This operation will let you see the mesh line. Using Meshing » Meshing » Surface Meshing function and select Tri3 option to create plane stress model by deleting all the unnecessary faces. Then, you can see the model after meshing: The process will be shown as below: A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro Meshing.SetMeshAttribute(crlPart=[Part(1)], surfaceMesh=SURFACE_MESH(dAvgElemSize=0.002, dMaxElemSize=0.003, dMinElemSize=0.0001, dGeomAngle=0.7853981634, dGeomMinSize=0.0001, iPerformanceMode=1, dAutoMergeTinyFacesAngle=0.5235987756, bGeomApprox=True, iNextEntityOffsetId=0)) Meshing.SurfaceMeshing(crlPart=[Part(1)], surfaceMesh=SURFACE_MESH(dAvgElemSize=0.002, dMaxElemSize=0.003, dMinElemSize=0.0001, dGeomAngle=0.7853981634, dGeomMinSize=0.0001, iPerformanceMode=1, dAutoMergeTinyFacesAngle=0.5235987756, bGeomApprox=True, iNextEntityOffsetId=0), iThreadNum=4) MeshEditAdjustVertex([3:1]) SetMeshAttrib([3:1], {0.002, 0.003, 0.0001, 1, 0.7853981634, 0.0001, 1.25, 0.1, 0.1, 0.7, 0.5, 1, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0.5235987756, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 10000000, 0, 0}) SurfaceMeshing2D([3:1], {0.002, 0.003, 0.0001, 1, 0.7853981634, 0.0001, 1.25, 0.1, 0.1, 0.7, 0.5, 1, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0.5235987756, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 10000000, 0, 0}, 1, 0, 4, 1, 0, 65280) note After executing Surface Meshing function, you need to convert the meshed model to first/second order. First order A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro ElementConv_Surface([3:1], 0) MeshEdit.SurfaceMesh(crlPart=[Part(1)], iType=0) Second order A corresponded PSJ-Command in the Python API window and Macro in the Macro window will be generated as below: PSJ-Command Macro ElementConv_Surface([3:1], 1) MeshEdit.SurfaceMesh(crlPart=[Part(1)])
