PSJ GUI EXAMPLES # --------------------- # This example demonstrades how to apply PSJ on a simple problem # such as plane stress problem # Required: Sunshine license #******************************************************************************* import JPT import re import os from pyjdg import * import random import ctypes import subprocess def cnvt_str_to_list(in_str: str) -> list: err_chars = r"/¥|^[]()" split_char = "," in_str = in_str.strip(err_chars) in_str = in_str.split(split_char) return in_str def convert_to_dbody(macro_tcursor: str): return JPT.CastDItemToDBody(JPT.MacroTCursorToDItem(str(macro_tcursor))) def create_geometry(part_name, get_width, get_height, get_radius): JPT.ClearLog() try: type_tobe_deleted = [3, 22] for type_id in type_tobe_deleted: for item in JPT.GetAllByTypeID(type_id): JPT.Exec('DeleteItem(0, [{0}:{1}], [], [], 1)'.format(type_id, item.id)) if part_name == "": part_name = "Plane_Stress_1" cube_size_x = float(get_width) * 0.001 cube_size_z = float(get_height) * 0.001 cube_size_h = 1e-3 hole_rad = float(get_radius) * 0.001 if cube_size_x > 0 and cube_size_z > 0 and hole_rad > 0: color = random.randint(10000, 60000000) create_cube = convert_to_dbody(Geometry.Part.Cube(dlLength=[cube_size_x, cube_size_h, cube_size_z], strName=part_name, iPartColor=color)) part_pos_x = 0 + cube_size_x / 2 part_pos_z = 0 + cube_size_z / 2 cylinder_height = cube_size_h + 2e-3 create_cylinder = Geometry.Part.Cylinder(dlOrigin=[part_pos_x, -0.001, part_pos_z], dTopRadius=hole_rad, dBottomRadius=hole_rad, dHeight=cylinder_height, iPartColor=color) # Get part ID Assemble.BooleanEx([Part(create_cube.id, max([_.id for _ in JPT.GetAllParts()]))], strNameSuffix="", iBooleanType=1) create_cube.name = part_name # Get ID of face all_face_id = [(str(_.typeID)) + ":" + (str(_.id)) for _ in JPT.GetAllFaces()] target_face = [] for cursor in all_face_id: str_command = 'EntityInfo({0},"CENTER")'.format(cursor) coordinate = cnvt_str_to_list(JPT.Exec(str_command))[1] # Select the coordinate value according to Y direction if float(coordinate) > 0: target_face.append(cursor) # Delete the unnecessary face res = [int(_.split(":")[-1]) for _ in target_face] # Change from list [6:1, 6:2, ...] --> list [1, 2] JPT.Exec('DeleteFace({}, 1)'.format(res)) JPT.ViewFitToModel() JPT.ClearLog() print("==================================================================") print("Created model information: ") print("--- Part name: %s" %str(part_name)) print("--- Width: %s mm" %str(get_width)) print("--- Height: %s mm" %str(get_height)) print("--- Hole radius: %s mm" %str(get_radius)) print("==================================================================") else: print("==================================================================") print("** [ERROR OCCURED] **") print("Inputted values are wrong, please check again!") print("The inputted values should follow the following rules:!") print("--- First: Model size should not be blanked. Its means you need to input float numbers") print("--- Second: The inputted values must be bigger than 0") print("==================================================================") except ValueError: print("==================================================================") print("** [ERROR OCCURED] **") print("Inputted values are wrong, please check again!") print("The inputted values should follow the following rules:!") print("--- First: Model size should not be blanked. Its means you need to input float numbers") print("--- Second: The inputted values must be bigger than 0") print("==================================================================") def clear_geometry(): JPT.ClearLog() for part in JPT.GetAllByTypeID(3): JPT.Exec('DeleteItem(0, [3:{}], [], [], 1)'.format(part.id)) JPT.ClearLog() print("==================================================================") print("Deleted all the created parts!") print("==================================================================") def generate_meshing(avg_size, min_size, max_size, second_element): try: JPT.ClearLog() JPT.Exec('ViewShowMesh(1)') avg_size_mm = float(avg_size) * 0.001 min_size_mm = float(min_size) * 0.001 max_size_mm = float(max_size) * 0.001 if min_size_mm < 0.7*avg_size_mm and min_size_mm > 0 and \ max_size_mm > 1.4*avg_size_mm and max_size_mm > 0 and \ avg_size_mm > 0: for part in JPT.GetAllParts(): Meshing.SurfaceMeshing(crlPart=[Part(part.id)], surfaceMesh=SURFACE_MESH(dAvgElemSize=avg_size_mm, dMaxElemSize=max_size_mm, dMinElemSize=min_size_mm, dGeomAngle=0.7853981634, dGeomMinSize=0.0001, dMinStretchVal=0.01, iPerformanceMode=1, dAutoMergeTinyFacesAngle=0.5235987756, bGeomApprox=True, iNextEntityOffsetId=0), iThreadNum=12) if second_element == True: MeshEdit.SurfaceMesh(crlPart=[Part(part.id)]) element_type = "Tri3 (First order)" if second_element == False else "Tri6 (Second order)" JPT.ClearLog() print("==================================================================") print("Meshed model information: ") print("--- Average size: %s mm" %str(avg_size)) print("--- Minimum size: %s mm" %str(min_size)) print("--- Maximum size: %s mm" %str(max_size)) print("--- Element type: %s" %str(element_type)) print("==================================================================") else: print("==================================================================") print("** [ERROR OCCURED] **") print("Inputted values are wrong, please check again!") print("The inputted values should In this tutorial, you'll learn how to export a simple report (pptx - Powerpoint format) by using python-pptx library with PSJ: Read the model information (part ID, part name, number of nodes, elements, faces, edges, etc.). Make a table comparing the above information. Append the content to a PowerPoint file with pre-defined template: First slide: title with created date. Second slide: model information table.

# Encoding for Japanese # coding: cp932 import JPT from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN from os.path import isfile, isdir from pptx import Presentation from pptx.util import Inches from pptx.util import Pt from pptx.enum.text import MSO_ANCHOR from datetime import datetime import re # Change your template and output folder here template_file = r"C:\Users\USERNAME\Documents\template\template_report.pptx" output_folder = r"C:\Users\USERNAME\Documents\template" def export_report(template_file = "", output_folder = "", num_of_cols = 8): if isfile(template_file) and isdir(output_folder): # Output report file template_file = re.sub(re.escape("\\"), "/", template_file) output_pptx_file = re.sub(re.escape("\\"), "/", output_folder + "/" + "modal_infor_report.pptx") # Open template report and store it to a parameter ppt_report = Presentation(template_file) # Create the first slide (Title slide) title_slide = ppt_report.slides.add_slide(ppt_report.slide_layouts[0]) title_slide.shapes.title.text = "EXAMPLE FOR EXPORTING MODAL INFORMATION" title_slide.placeholders[1].text = "Created: " + \ str(datetime.now().year) + \ "." + \ str(datetime.now().month) + \ "." + \ str(datetime.now().day) # Create the 2nd slide (Modal info slide) slide = ppt_report.slides.add_slide(ppt_report.slide_layouts[4]) slide.shapes.title.text = "MODAL INFORMATION" x, y, cx, cy = Inches(0.5), Inches(1.2), Inches(10), Inches(2) table = slide.shapes.add_table(len(JPT.GetAllParts()) + 2, num_of_cols, x, y, cx, cy).table table.cell(0, 0).merge(table.cell(0, num_of_cols - 1)) table.cell(0, 0).text = "Modal information" table.cell(1, 0).text = "Part ID" table.cell(1, 1).text = "Part Name" table.cell(1, 2).text = "No. of Faces" table.cell(1, 3).text = "No. of Edges" table.cell(1, 4).text = "No. of Elements" table.cell(1, 5).text = "No. of Nodes" table.cell(1, 6).text = "Range of Node ID" table.cell(1, 7).text = "Range of Element ID" table.columns[0].width = Inches(1.2) table.columns[1].width = Inches(1.9) table.columns[2].width = Inches(1.2) table.columns[3].width = Inches(1.2) table.columns[4].width = Inches(1.5) table.columns[5].width = Inches(1.5) table.columns[6].width = Inches(1.9) table.columns[7].width = Inches(1.9) if len(JPT.GetAllParts()): for row, part in enumerate(JPT.GetAllParts()): table.cell(row + 2, 0).text = str(part.id) table.cell(row + 2, 1).text = part.name table.cell(row + 2, 2).text = str(len(part.faces)) table.cell(row + 2, 3).text = str(len(part.edges)) table.cell(row + 2, 4).text = str(len(part.elems)) table.cell(row + 2, 5).text = str(len(part.nodes)) table.cell(row + 2, 6).text = "Max: " + \ str(max([_.id for _ in part.nodes])) + \ "\n" + \ "Min: " + \ str(min([_.id for _ in part.nodes])) table.cell(row + 2, 7).text = "Max: " + \ str(max([_.id for _ in part.elems])) + \ "\n" + \ "Min: " + \ str(min([_.id for _ in part.elems])) table.rows[row].height = Inches(0.53) for row in table.rows: for cell in row.cells: cell.vertical_anchor = MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE for paragraph in cell.text_frame.paragraphs: paragraph.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER for run in paragraph.runs: run.font.size = Pt(13) run.font.name = "MS UI Gothic" ppt_report.save(output_pptx_file) print(" FINISHED ".center(100, "*")) else: print("Error: template file and/or output folder does not exist!") Get and display total 2D elements having Shell Property at Python API window. Get and display total 1D elements having Beam Property at Python API window. Please prepare analysis model having 1D/2D elements in advance, below script in this tutorial didn't include analysis model. Target entity of 2D property in analysis model should be 'Face' entity.

# Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Get list of all 'Face' and 'Edge' entities in model listFace = JPT.GetAllFaces() listEdge = JPT.GetAllEdges() # Get list of 'Shell' and 'Beam' Property in model listShellProp = JPT.GetAllByType(JPT.DItemType.PROPERTY_2D_SHELL) listBeamProp = JPT.GetAllByType(JPT.DItemType.PROPERTY_1D_BEAM) # Define function to check whether face has 'Shell' Property or not by face's ID def CheckFaceHasShellProperty(faceID): for prop in listShellProp: targetFace = prop.targets for face in targetFace: if face.id == faceID: return faceID # Define function to get total 2D elements having 'Shell' Property def Get2DElemFromShellProperty(): list2DElem = [] for face in listFace: if CheckFaceHasShellProperty(face.id) != None: dItemFaces = JPT.GetEntitiesByID(JPT.DItemType.FACE, face.id) for item in dItemFaces: FaceElems = JPT.CastDItemToDFace(item).elems print("{} elements are extracted from Face ID {} having Shell Property ".\ format(len(FaceElems),face.id)) for elem in FaceElems: list2DElem.append(elem) return list2DElem # Define function to check whether edge has 'Beam' Property or not by edge's ID def CheckEdgeHasBeamProperty(edgeID): for prop in listBeamProp: targetEdge = prop.targets for edge in targetEdge: if edge.id == edgeID: return edgeID # Define function to get total 1D elements having 'Beam' Property def Get1DElemFromBeamProperty(): list1DElem = [] for edge in listEdge: if CheckEdgeHasBeamProperty(edge.id) != None: dItemEdges = JPT.GetEntitiesByID(JPT.DItemType.EDGE, edge.id) for item in dItemEdges: BeamElems = JPT.CastDItemToDEdge(item).elems print("{} elements are extracted from Edge ID {} having Beam Property ".\ format(len(BeamElems),edge.id)) for elem in BeamElems: list1DElem.append(elem) return list1DElem # Get and display total 2D elements having 'Shell' Property at Python API window listElem2D = Get2DElemFromShellProperty() print("Total 2D elements have Shell Property: {}".format(len(listElem2D))) JPT.Debugger(listElem2D) # Get and display total 1D elements having 'Beam' Property at Python API window listElem1D = Get1DElemFromBeamProperty() print("Total 1D elements have Beam Property: {}".format(len(listElem1D))) JPT.Debugger(listElem1D)

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to get database information from part: Load sample model at installed Jupiter path into Jupiter. Get information of first part in all parts list, assign to part. Display name, id of part at Python API window. Change Name / Color / Mesh Color/ Transparency of part. Get entities (Face/Edge/Vertex/Element/Node) of part. Get Material and Property of part. Get Load and BC / Connection / Local Mesh Setting / Contact related to part. Get Area / Volume / Mass / Center of Gravity / Moment of Inertia of part.

# Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Get installed jupiter, sample path # Then load sample model into Jupiter jupiterPath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.PROGRAM_PATH) samplePath = jupiterPath + '/SampleData/PSJ/PSJ-Utility/JtdbSample/Get_Infor_Part_Sample.jtdb' FileMenu.LoadJTDB(strFileName=samplePath) # Fit view of model on display view JPT.ViewFitToModel() # Get list of all parts in current model listpart = JPT.GetAllParts() # Get information of first part in all parts list, assign to 'part' # Then display name, id of first part at Python API window part = listpart[0] JPT.Debugger(part) print (part.id) print (part.name) # Change name of 'part' part.name = "change_name_of_first_part" # Change color of 'part' with random color part.color = JPT.GetRandomJPTColor() # Change color of 'part' with with RGB color part.color = JPT.ConvertRGBToJPTColor(255,0,0) # Change mesh line color of 'part' with RGB color part.colorMesh = JPT.ConvertRGBToJPTColor(255,255,255) # Set transparency of 'part' as 50% part.transparency = 50 # Get all faces from 'part' listFaces = part.faces JPT.Debugger(listFaces) # Get all elements from 'part' listElems = part.elems JPT.Debugger(listElems) # Get all nodes from 'part' listNodes = part.nodes JPT.Debugger(listNodes) # Get all edges from 'part' listEdges = part.edges JPT.Debugger(listEdges) # Get all vertex from 'part' listVertex = part.vertex JPT.Debugger(listVertex) # Get material from 'part' # Then display ID, name of material at Python API window listMaterials = part.materials if len(listMaterials) == 0: print ("This part has no material assignment.") else: for material in listMaterials: print ("material id of 'part': " + str(material.id)) print ("material name of 'part': " + str(material.name)) # Get properties from 'part' # Then display ID, name of properties at Python API window listProperties = part.properties if len(listProperties) == 0: print ("This part has no properties assignment.") else: for property in listProperties: print ("property id of 'part': " + str(property.id)) print ("property name of 'part': " + str(property.name)) # Get all Load and BCs related to 'part' # Then display ID, name of Load and BCs at Python API window listLoadAndBCs = part.loadAndBCs if len(listLoadAndBCs) == 0: print ("This part has no related Load and Boundary Condition.") else: for loadAndBC in listLoadAndBCs: print ("loadAndBC id related to 'part': " + str(loadAndBC.id)) print ("loadAndBC name related to 'part': " + str(loadAndBC.name)) # Get all connections related to 'part' # Then display ID, name of connections at Python API window listConnections = part.connections if len(listConnections) == 0: print ("This part has no related connection(MPC/RBE2).") else: for connection in listConnections: print ("connection id related to 'part': " + str(connection.id)) print ("connection name related to 'part': " + str(connection.name)) # Get all localMeshSettings from 'part' # Then display ID, name of localMeshSettings at Python API window listLocalMeshSettings = part.localMeshSettings if len(listLocalMeshSettings) == 0: print ("This part has no local mesh setting.") else: for localMeshSetting in listLocalMeshSettings: print ("localMeshSetting id of 'part': " + str(localMeshSetting.id)) print ("localMeshSetting name of 'part': " + str(localMeshSetting.name)) # Get all contacts related to 'part' # Then display ID, name of contacts at Python API window listContacts = part.contacts if len(listContacts) == 0: print ("This part has no related contact.") else: for contact in listContacts: print ("contact id related to 'part': " + str(contact.id)) print ("contact name related to 'part': " + str(contact.name)) # Get and display area value of 'part' at Python API window print("Area of 'part': " + str(part.area)) # Get and display volume value of 'part' at Python API window print("Volume of 'part': " + str(part.volume)) # Get and display mass value of 'part' at Python API window print("Mass of 'part': " + str(part.mass)) # Get and display center of gravity value of 'part' at Python API window print("Center of Gravity of 'part': [%s %s %s] " % \ (str(part.gravityCenter.x) , str(part.gravityCenter.y), str(part.gravityCenter.z))) # Get and display moment of inertia value of 'part' at Python API window print("Moment of Inertia of 'part': " ) JPT.Debugger(part.momentInertia)

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to get database info from entity: Load sample model at installed Jupiter path into Jupiter. Get list of entity (local face setting / pressure / group) from model database, then display name, id, entity type and target ID of each entity. Get list of entity (element / face) by target entity ID from model database, then change color of each target entity.

# Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Get installed jupiter, sample path. Load sample model into Jupiter jupiterPath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.PROGRAM_PATH) samplePath = jupiterPath + '/SampleData/PSJ/PSJ-Utility/JtdbSample/EntityModel.jtdb' FileMenu.LoadJTDB(samplePath) JPT.ViewFitToModel() # Get list of 'local face setting' entity from model database # Then display name, id, entity type and all faces ID of local setting listLocalSetting = JPT.GetAllByType(JPT.DItemType.LOCAL_SETTING) if listLocalSetting.sizeVec() > 0: for ls in listLocalSetting: print ("local setting name: " + ls.name) print ("local setting ID: " + str(ls.id)) print ("entity type: " + str(ls.type)) listTargetFaces = ls.targets print ("target face ID of local face setting list:") for face in listTargetFaces: print(face.id) # Get list of 'general pressure' entity from model database # Then display name, id, entity type and all faces ID of general pressure listGeneralPressure = JPT.GetAllByType(JPT.DItemType.LBC_G_PRESSURE) if listGeneralPressure.sizeVec() > 0: for pressure in listGeneralPressure: print ("pressure name: " + pressure.name) print ("pressure ID: " + str(pressure.id)) print ("entity type: " + str(pressure.type)) listTargetFaces = pressure.targets print ("target face ID of general pressure list:") for face in listTargetFaces: print(face.id) # Get list of 'group' entity from model database # Then display name, id, entity type and all element ID of group listGroup = JPT.GetAllByType(JPT.DItemType.GROUP) if listGroup.sizeVec() > 0: for group in listGroup: print ("group name: " + group.name) print ("group id: " + str(group.id)) print ("entity type: " + str(group.type)) listTargetElems = group.targets print ("target element ID of element group entity list:") for elem in listTargetElems: print(elem.id) # Get list of 'element' entity with ID 239 from model database # Then change color of element ID 239 to white listElemEntityObject = JPT.GetEntitiesByID(JPT.DItemType.ELEM, 239) if listElemEntityObject.sizeVec() == 1: elemObject = JPT.CastDItemToDFace(listElemEntityObject[0]) elemObject.color = JPT.ConvertRGBToJPTColor(255, 255, 255) # Get list of 'face' entity with ID 23 from model database # Then change color of face ID 23 to green listFaceEntityObject = JPT.GetEntitiesByID(JPT.DItemType.FACE, 23) if listFaceEntityObject.sizeVec() == 1: faceObject = JPT.CastDItemToDFace(listFaceEntityObject[0]) faceObject.color = JPT.ConvertRGBToJPTColor(0, 255, 0)

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to get related Jupiter path information: Get Jupiter Internal Path: Get related Jupiter internal path information, such as: Jupiter installation folder path, material library path, temp folder path, etc. Get Loaded Module or File Path: Get loaded module or file path information that Jupiter uses. Get Jupiter Internal Path Get Loaded Module or File Path List all Jupiter paths information at Python API window. List all path types at Python API window. Get related Jupiter paths: installation path, current opening .jtdb file path, material library path, IDE database path, etc. 🧮 Usability​ In order to get the full path of the loaded file, using JPT.PATHTYPE.FILE_PATH will solve the problem. 🪁 Usage Environment​ In IDE, use the Open (File » Open) option to load script from file. In File Launcher, use the register button S to load a file. For details, see the File Launcher. In Customized Function, put the script in PSJ-Command custom folder, Jupiter will return the path of itself.
In order to get the full path of the loaded file, using JPT.PATHTYPE.FILE_PATH will solve the problem.

In IDE, use the Open (File » Open) option to load script from file. In File Launcher, use the register button S to load a file. For details, see the File Launcher. In Customized Function, put the script in PSJ-Command custom folder, Jupiter will return the path of itself.

Get Jupiter Internal Path Get Loaded Module or File Path # Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # List all Jupiter paths information at Python API window JPT.PrintAppPathInfo() # List all path types at Python API window JPT.Debugger(JPT.PathType.values) # Get Jupiter installation path programPath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.PROGRAM_PATH) print(programPath) # Get Jupiter temp path tempPath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.TEMP_PATH) print(tempPath) # Get Jupiter app data path appdataPath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.APPDATA_PATH) print(appdataPath) # Get current opening document file path docPath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.DOC_PATH) print(docPath) # Get default material library path materialLibPath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.MATERIAL_LIB_FILE_PATH) print(materialLibPath) # Get user-defined material library path materialUserPath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.MATERIAL_USER_FILE_PATH) print(materialUserPath) # Get Jupiter database path databasePath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.DATABASE_PATH) print(databasePath) # Get Sunshine path sunshinePath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.SUNSHINE_PATH) print(sunshinePath) # Get IDE database path ideDataPath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.IDE_DATA_PATH) print(ideDataPath) # Get folder path for custom ribbon by PSJ psjRibbonPath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.PSJ_COMMAND_PATH) print(psjRibbonPath) """ Sample script for putting on the loaded file """ # Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Get loaded file path filePath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.FILE_PATH) print(filePath)

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to get log from Output window, Macro window and Python API window: Get log content at Macro window. Then create a macro file .jpl to save Macro log content. Get log content at Python API window. Then create a file .log to save Python API log content. Get log content at Output window. Then create a file .log to save Output log content.

# Get log content at Macro window # Create a macro file .jpl to save Macro log content logMacro = JPT.GetMacroLog() print(logMacro) fileMacro = open("D:/Macro.jpl", "w") for line in logMacro: fileMacro.write(line) fileMacro.close() # Get log content at Python API window # Create a file .log to save Python API log content logAPI = JPT.GetPythonAPILog() print(logAPI) fileAPI = open("D:/PythonAPI.log", "w") for line in logAPI: fileAPI.write(line) fileAPI.close() # Get log content at Output window # Create a file .log to save Output log content logOutput = JPT.GetOutputLog() print(logOutput) fileOutput = open("D:/Output.log", "w") for line in logOutput: fileOutput.write(line) fileOutput.close()

Looping through each part of all parts list, then display id, name, area of each part at Python API window. Write log content of Python API window to a file for backup.

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to get nearest node ID from a floating node in the model: Define a function to get distance between 2 nodes. Get node object from floating node by user-defined ID 489. Get list of all nodes in current model. Looping through all nodes (except floatingNode) in model, find node has minimum distance with floating node. Display nearest node's ID with floating node 489 at Python API window.

# Import 'sys' module of Python import sys # Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Create sample model (a cube and a floating node with ID=489) Geometry.Part.Cube() MeshEdit.CreateNode.Absolute(veclNodeCoord=[[0.0101, 0.0055, 0.0055]], ilNewNodeID=[489]) # Fit view of model on display view JPT.ViewFitToModel() # Define a function to measure distance between 2 nodes def distance_between_two_node(one,two) : return (((two.x-one.x)**2)+((two.y-one.y)**2)+((two.z-one.z)**2))**(1/2) # Get node object from floating node object by ID, convert DItem to DNode idFloatingNode = 489 itemNode = JPT.GetEntitiesByID(JPT.DItemType.NODE, idFloatingNode) floatingNode = JPT.CastDItemToDNode(itemNode[0]) # Get list of all nodes in current model all_nodes = JPT.GetAllNodes() # Looping through all nodes (except floatingNode) in current model # Check to find node has minimum distance with floating node min = sys.float_info.max for node in all_nodes: if node.id == floatingNode.id: continue dis = distance_between_two_node(node.pos, floatingNode.pos) if dis < min: min = dis nearestNode = node # Display nearest node's ID at Python API window print("ID of nearest node with floating node is: {}".format(nearestNode.id))

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to get property from part's ID: Create material for property. Create 2 Shell properties: first is for first cube part, second is for second and third cube parts. Get list of all parts and 2D Shell properties in current model. Define a function to get property from ID of part. Get property from part ID. Display property ID, property name, part ID, part name corresponding at Python API window.

# Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Create 3 cube parts cube1 = Geometry.Part.Cube(iPartColor=12999622) cube2 = Geometry.Part.Cube(dlOrigin=[0.01, 0.0, 0.0], dlLength=[0.02, 0.01, 0.01], strName="Cube_2", iPartColor=5093709) cube3 = Geometry.Part.Cube(dlOrigin=[0.03, 0.0, 0.0], dlLength=[0.03, 0.01, 0.01], strName="Cube_3", iPartColor=6118877) # Fit view of model on display view JPT.ViewFitToModel() # Create material Properties.Material.Add("Structural_Steel", [Density([(DENSITY, 7.85e-09)]), Elastic([(YOUNGS_MODULUS, 200000.0), (POISSONS_RATIO, 0.3)])]) # Create 2 Shell properties. First is for Cube1 part. Second is for Cube2 and Cube3 parts Properties.Shell(strName="Shell Property 1 for Cube1", iPropertyId=1, dThickness=0.005, crlTargets=[cube1], crMatMembrane=Material(1), crMatBend=Material(1), crMatShear=Material(1) ) Properties.Shell(strName="Shell Property 2 for Cube2-3", iPropertyId=2, dThickness=0.01, crlTargets=[cube2, cube3], crMatMembrane=Material(1), crMatBend=Material(1), crMatShear=Material(1) ) # Get list of all parts and 2D Shell properties in current model listPart = JPT.GetAllParts() listProp = JPT.GetAllByType(JPT.DItemType.PROPERTY_2D_SHELL) # Define a function to get property from ID of part def GetPropertyFromPartID(partID): for prop in listProp: listAssosicatedPart = prop.targets for assoPart in listAssosicatedPart: if assoPart.id == partID: return prop # Get property from ID of part by looping through each part of all parts list # Display part name, property ID, property name for each part at Python API window for part in listPart: foundProperty = GetPropertyFromPartID(part.id) print("Property ID: {} | Property Name: {} | Part ID: {} | Part Name: {} " .format(foundProperty.id,foundProperty.name,part.id,part.name))

# Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() ############ CASE 1 : return value from a single entity ############ # Get return value when create new cube part, Geometry.Part.Cube() will return a single object with two attributes: # In this tutorial, you'll learn how to estimate the value of Pi using Monte Carlo method, by: Python built-in function. Numba library. Using Numba, the calculation can speed up from 40 to 100 times. Numba translates Python functions to optimized machine code at runtime using the industry-standard LLVM compiler library. Numba-compiled numerical algorithms in Python can approach the speeds of C or FORTRAN. You don't need to replace the Python interpreter, run a separate compilation step, or even have a C/C++ compiler installed. Just apply one of the Numba decorators to your Python function, and Numba does the rest.

Python built-in function Numba library import random import timeit def monte_carlo_pi(nsamples): acc = 0 for i in range(nsamples): x = random.random() y = random.random() if (x ** 2 + y ** 2) < 1.0: acc += 1 return 4.0 * acc / nsamples start = timeit.default_timer() value = monte_carlo_pi(100_000_000) stop = timeit.default_timer() print('Estimate {0:.6f} within {1:.3f} seconds'.format(value, stop - start)) import random import timeit from numba import jit @jit(nopython=True) def monte_carlo_pi(nsamples): acc = 0 for i in range(nsamples): x = random.random() y = random.random() if (x ** 2 + y ** 2) < 1.0: acc += 1 return 4.0 * acc / nsamples start = timeit.default_timer() value = monte_carlo_pi(100_000_000) stop = timeit.default_timer() print('Estimate {0:.6f} within {1:.3f} seconds'.format(value, stop - start))

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to extend PSJ capability by installing new Python library which is not installed by default: Install new Python library using pip. Check if new library is already installed. Try running PSJ using new installed library.

Prepare below .bat file and execute it on your machine: set PYTHONLIB=%APPDATA%\TechnoStar\JPT5.1.0\PythonLib\Lib set PYTHONPACKAGE=%PYTHONLIB%\site-packages set PYTHONDLL=%APPDATA%\TechnoStar\JPT5.1.0\PythonLib\DLLs set PYTHONHOME=C:\Program Files\TechnoStar\Jupiter_5.1 set PYTHONPATH=%PYTHONHOME%;%PYTHONLIB%;%PYTHONPACKAGE%;%PYTHONDLL% "%PYTHONHOME%\python.exe" -m pip install -t "%PYTHONPACKAGE%" <package_name> For example, if you want to install plotly library to Jupiter v5.1, prepare below .bat file and double click the file. set PYTHONLIB=%APPDATA%\TechnoStar\JPT5.1.0\PythonLib\Lib set PYTHONPACKAGE=%PYTHONLIB%\site-packages set PYTHONDLL=%APPDATA%\TechnoStar\JPT5.1.0\PythonLib\DLLs set PYTHONHOME=C:\Program Files\TechnoStar\Jupiter_5.1 set PYTHONPATH=%PYTHONHOME%;%PYTHONLIB%;%PYTHONPACKAGE%;%PYTHONDLL% "%PYTHONHOME%\python.exe" -m pip install -t "%PYTHONPACKAGE%" -U plotly You can check if plotly has been installed by using below command in Jupiter built-in IDE. import plotly print(plotly.__version__) You can also try testing PSJ with plotly using below sample: import plotly.graph_objects as go from plotly.subplots import make_subplots # Equation of ring cyclide # see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dupin_cyclide import numpy as np a, b, d = 1.32, 1., 0.8 c = a**2 - b**2 u, v = np.mgrid[0:2*np.pi:100j, 0:2*np.pi:100j] x = (d * (c - a * np.cos(u) * np.cos(v)) + b**2 * np.cos(u)) / (a - c * np.cos(u) * np.cos(v)) y = b * np.sin(u) * (a - d*np.cos(v)) / (a - c * np.cos(u) * np.cos(v)) z = b * np.sin(v) * (c*np.cos(u) - d) / (a - c * np.cos(u) * np.cos(v)) fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, specs=[[{'is_3d': True}, {'is_3d': True}]], subplot_titles=['Color corresponds to z', 'Color corresponds to distance to origin'], ) fig.add_trace(go.Surface(x=x, y=y, z=z, colorbar_x=-0.07), 1, 1) fig.add_trace(go.Surface(x=x, y=y, z=z, surfacecolor=x**2 + y**2 + z**2), 1, 2) fig.update_layout(title_text="Ring cyclide") fig.show()

Create a String Vector containing parser pattern. Introduce two methods to parse string result. Introduce how to convert return result from macro to Jupiter database object.

# Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Sample return result from macro sampleReturn = '"string", 3:1, 10:210-10:202, [10:210-10:202, 10:316-10:308], \ [10:210, 10:202, 10:316 ,10:308], [[10:210], [10:210, 10:202], [10:316 ,10:308]], \ ["string1", "string2", "string3"], [1,2,3], [1,2,3,4,5,6], 0.12345' # Create a cube Geometry.Part.Cube(strName="Cube_1", iPartColor=12999622) JPT.ViewFitToModel() # Create a String Vector containing parser pattern. Example: "string", "number", "list_cursor" # ********************************************************************************************* # Below is example of String Data Rules for parser pattern: # string : "string example" # cursor : 3:1 # cursor_pair : 10:210-10:202 # list_cursor_pair : [10:210-10:202, 10:316-10:308] # list_cursor : [10:210, 10:202, 10:316 ,10:308] # list_list_cursor : [[10:210], [10:210, 10:202], [10:316 ,10:308]] # list_string : ["string1", "string2", "string3"] # vector3d : [1,2,3] # list_number : [1,2,3,4,5,6] # number : 0.12345 # ********************************************************************************************* ArgPatterns = JPT.StringVector() ArgPatterns.append("string") ArgPatterns.append("cursor") ArgPatterns.append("cursor_pair") ArgPatterns.append("list_cursor_pair") ArgPatterns.append("list_cursor") ArgPatterns.append("list_list_cursor") ArgPatterns.append("list_string") ArgPatterns.append("vector3d") ArgPatterns.append("list_number") ArgPatterns.append("number") # In this tutorial, you'll learn how to manipulate PagesCtrl and PageItem components: Create a PagesCtrl component. Select a PageItem. Based on selected PageItem, we can trigger events to get name or to show the information of PageItem.

# Encoding for Japanese # coding: cp932 from pyjdg import * def on_pageitem_changed(dlg,name,old_page): current_page=dlg.get_pagesctrl_current_page(name="PagesCtrl1") current_page_name=dlg.get_pagesctrl_page_name(name="PagesCtrl1", page_index=current_page) old_page_name=dlg.get_pagesctrl_page_name(name="PagesCtrl1", page_index=old_page) print("Selected page name : " + current_page_name) print("Previous selected page : " + old_page_name) def main(): dlg=JDGCreator(title="Dialog",resizable=True,validation=True) dlg.add_pagesctrl(name="PagesCtrl1",width=200,height=200,layout="Window") dlg.add_pageitem(name="PagesCtrl1",page_name="PageItem2", page_header="PageItem1") dlg.add_pageitem(name="PagesCtrl1",page_name="PageItem3", page_header="PageItem2") dlg.add_pageitem(name="PagesCtrl1",page_name="PageItem4", page_header="PageItem3") dlg.add_hlayout(name="footer",layout="Window") dlg.add_space(orientation="horizontal",layout="footer") dlg.add_button(name="Ok",text="Ok",layout="footer") dlg.add_button(name="ButtonCancel",text="Cancel",layout="footer") dlg.add_space(orientation="horizontal",layout="footer") dlg.generate_window() dlg.on_pagesctrl_active_page(name="PagesCtrl1",callfunc=on_pageitem_changed) if __name__=='__main__': main()

Create message box with information-Yes-No-Cancel type. Get and display the return value of message box button from user's selection in Python API window.

# Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Display all message box types in Python API window JPT.Debugger(JPT.MsgBoxType.values) # Create message box with information-yes-no-cancel type, # use "answer" to store return value of message box from user answer = JPT.MessageBoxPSJ("Input information: content of the message", JPT.MsgBoxType.MB_INFORMATION_YESNOCANCEL) # Get and display the return value of message box from user in Python API window if answer == "YES": print ("You selected 'Yes' button") elif answer == "NO": print ("You selected 'No' button") else: print ("You selected 'Cancel' button")

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to plot models' information (number of nodes, elements, edges, faces, etc.) using matplotlib library.: Read part name, number of faces, edges, elements and nodes from all parts. Plot the above information to a bar chart or line graph for comparison. This plot can be exported to a picture file and import into MS PowerPoint automatically by PSJ.

Bar chart Line graph # Encoding for Japanese # coding: cp932 # Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Make 4 sample models (if you already had a model opened, ignore the below code) Geometry.Part.Cube(ilAxialNodes=[90, 70, 50]) Geometry.Part.Cylinder(dlOrigin=[0.03, 0.0, 0.0], dTopOuterRadius=0.005, dBottomOuterRadius=0.005, dHeight=0.03, iCircularNodes=100, iAxialNodes=300, iPartColor=6409934) Geometry.Part.Sphere(dlOrigin=[0.06, 0.0, 0.0], iLatitudeDivisions=100, iLongitudeDivisions=400, iPartColor=13259210) Geometry.Part.Torus(dlOrigin=[0.12, 0.0, 0.0], iCircumNodes=100, iRingNodes=300, iPartColor=7697908) ############################################################################################# #################################### Start the main code #################################### ############################################################################################# import numpy as np import matplotlib.pyplot as plt def auto_label(rects): """ Attach a text label above each bar in *rects*, displaying its height. """ for rect in rects: ax.annotate('{}'.format(rect.get_height()), xy = (rect.get_x() + rect.get_width() / 2, rect.get_height()), xytext = (0, 3), textcoords = "offset points", ha = "center", va = "center", size = 8) # Start plotting with matplotlib labels = [] part_info = [] for part in JPT.GetAllParts(): labels.append(part.name) part_info.append([part.name, len(part.faces), len(part.edges), len(part.elems), len(part.nodes)]) x = np.arange(len(labels)) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize = (8, 6)) ax.set_ylabel("Total values") ax.set_title("Comparision between parts existing on the model") ax.set_xticks(x) ax.set_xticklabels(labels, rotation = 'vertical') ax.autoscale(axis="both") for i in range(len(part_info)): rect_1 = ax.bar(x[i], part_info[i][3], 0.3, color = "magenta", label = part_info[i][0]) auto_label(rect_1) rect_2 = ax.bar(x[i], part_info[i][4], 0.3, color = "gold", label = part_info[i][0]) auto_label(rect_2) ax.legend((rect_1, rect_2), ("Number of elements", "Number of nodes"), bbox_to_anchor = (1.05, 1), loc = "upper left", fancybox = True, framealpha = 1, shadow = True, borderpad = 1) fig.tight_layout() plt.show() # Encoding for Japanese # coding: cp932 # Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Make 4 sample models (if you already had a model opened, ignore the below code) Geometry.Part.Cube(ilAxialNodes=[90, 70, 50]) Geometry.Part.Cylinder(dlOrigin=[0.03, 0.0, 0.0], dTopOuterRadius=0.005, dBottomOuterRadius=0.005, dHeight=0.03, iCircularNodes=100, iAxialNodes=300, iPartColor=6409934) Geometry.Part.Sphere(dlOrigin=[0.06, 0.0, 0.0], iLatitudeDivisions=100, iLongitudeDivisions=400, iPartColor=13259210) Geometry.Part.Torus(dlOrigin=[0.12, 0.0, 0.0], iCircumNodes=100, iRingNodes=300, iPartColor=7697908) ############################################################################################# #################################### Start the main code #################################### ############################################################################################# import numpy as np import matplotlib.pyplot as plt # Start plotting with matplotlib labels = [] part_info = [] for part in JPT.GetAllParts(): labels.append(part.name) part_info.append([part.name, len(part.faces), len(part.edges), len(part.elems), len(part.nodes)]) x = np.arange(len(labels)) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=[10, 8]) ax.set_ylabel("Total values") ax.set_title("Comparision between parts existing on the model") ax.set_xticks(x) ax.set_xticklabels(labels, rotation = 'vertical') y_elem = [] y_node = [] for i in range(len(part_info)): y_elem.append(part_info[i][3]) y_node.append(part_info[i][4]) line_1 = ax.plot(x, y_elem, marker='o', color = "magenta", label='Number of elements') line_2 = ax.plot(x, y_node, marker='x', color = "gold", label='Number of nodes') for i in range(len(y_elem)): ax.annotate(y_elem[i], (x[i], y_elem[i]), size=8) ax.annotate(y_node[i], (x[i], y_node[i]), size=8) ax.legend(['Number of elements', 'Number of nodes'], bbox_to_anchor = (1.05, 1), loc = "upper left", fancybox = True, framealpha = 1, shadow = True, borderaxespad=0., borderpad = 1) plt.gcf().subplots_adjust(right=0.75) plt.show()

This document introduces the use of external files in Python with examples. Basic operations The case if characters garbled (character encoding) String processing CSV file processing File path expressions and separators Tips for obtaining files and folders (os module)

Prepare a Sample.txt file with the following contents under C:\Temp beforehand. #Number,Type,ID,Value 1,Node,5,300 2,Node,6,800 3,Element,8,4.65 The open function in Python is used. Typical uses of the open function include the following Prepare a variable that points to the contents of a file, and read and display it line by line with the readline function. Filepath='C:/Temp/Sample.txt' with open(Filepath,'r') as fr: print(fr.readline()) print(fr.readline()) print(fr.readline()) print(fr.readline()) The contents of the file are read and displayed line by line until the end with a for statement. Filepath='C:/Temp/Sample.txt' for line in open(Filepath,'r'): print(line) Prepare a variable that points to the contents of the file, and read and display it line by line with the readline function. Filepath='C:/Temp/Sample.txt' with open(Filepath,'r') as fr: while line := fr.readline(): print(line) Prepare a variable that points to the contents of the file, read multiple lines at once with resdlines, and display what is stored in the list. Filepath='C:/Temp/Sample.txt' with open(Filepath,'r') as fr: print(fr.readlines()) Another way is to provide a variable that points to the contents of the file. In this case, you must explicitly close the file with close when you are finished reading it. Filepath='C:/Temp/Sample.txt' fr = open(Filepath,'r') print(fr.readlines()) fr.close()

Create MyNewFile.txt under C:\Temp and output the string. Filepath='C:/Temp/MyNewFile.txt' with open(Filepath,'w') as fw: fw.write('Export string: first line\n') fw.write('Export string: second line\n')
documents.s: Write out to a new file

documents.t: Append strings to the existing file MyNewFile.txt under C:\Temp Filepath='C:/Temp/MyNewFile.txt' with open(Filepath,'a') as fw: fw.write('Export string: third line\n') fw.write('Export string: fourth line\n')

When coding in Python, the character encoding of the operating system is used. For Japanese OS, Shift-JIS is used, and for English OS, UTF-8 is used. Therefore, if you have a problem with garbled characters when reading a file in Python, you can specify the encoding with "encoding" when opening the file to avoid garbled characters. *This problem mainly happens only if you use wide characters. import os Folder = 'C:/Temp' #エンコードUTF-8のファイル File = 'UTF-8.txt' path = os.path.join(Folder, File) for line in open(path,'r',encoding='utf8'): print(line)

When a string from a file is read, even line breaks and whitespace before and after the string are read as is. Python has many useful string processing functions. Here are some of them. import os for line in open('C:/Temp/Sample.txt','r'): #Skip readline if the string contains "Element" if 'Element' in line: continue #Remove consecutive whitespace characters (full/half-width spaces, tabs, line feeds) before and after a string line_correct=line.strip() #Replace the specified character (replacing it with a space character will result in deletion) plane_line=line_correct.replace('#','') #Split string with comma as delimiter and input into list data=plane_line.split(',') print(data)

When expressing a file path in Python code, the path separator is the "/" (slash) character. In Windowsv OS, the "" (backslash or "￥")is used to express a path separator, but this symbol is considered a special character in Python code, so you need to change it to one of the following notations. #Separater of python. Filepath='C:/Temp/MyFile.txt' #The backslash is used as a file path separator by writing the special character backslash twice. Filepath='C:\\Temp\\MyFile.txt' #Use Windows file path delimiters with raw strings. Filepath=r'C:\Temp\MyFile.txt' #In this notation, a backslash cannot be used at the end of a path because the ' at the end of a line cannot be recognized as a special character. #NG example #Folderpath=r'C:\Temp\'

Since file paths are strings, you can use the union of strings when concatenating file paths, but To safely concatenate file paths, it is recommended to import the os module and use the os.path.join() function. For example, the following can be used without error by adding the path separator used by each OS in the appropriate position. import os Folder = 'C:/Temp' File = 'Sample.txt' path = os.path.join(Folder, File) print(path)

The os module is a python module for using os-dependent functions and has a number of functions that are particularly useful for file and folder manipulation. Here are some examples of common uses. #use os module import os #Confirm existence of paths (files/folders) isExists=os.path.exists(r'C:\Temp\MyFile.txt') print(isExists) #Determines if the specified path is a file - Used to check for the existence of a file isFile=os.path.isfile(r'C:\Temp\Sample.txt') print(isFile) #Determines if the specified path is a folder - Used to confirm the existence of a folder isDir=os.path.isdir(r'C:\Temp') print(isDir) #Store files in the specified folder in a list fileList=os.listdir('C:\Temp') for file in fileList: print(file) #Get folder/file tree under the specified folder for currFolder,folders,files in os.walk('C:\Temp'): print(currFolder) print(folders) print(files)

Import all necessary PSJ modules. Example: check.py import JPT import Geometry Geometry.Part.Cube() JPT.ViewFitToModel() faces = JPT.GetAllFaces() for face in faces: JPT.SelectionByID(JPT.EntityType.FACE, face.id, True)

Example command: "C:\Program Files\TechnoStar\Jupiter_5.0.3\python.exe" -m py_compile C:\Temp\check.py A folder named __pycache__ will be created in the same location as check.py, and a file named check.cpython-39.pyc will be generated inside it.

# Load and execute the .pyc file import importlib.util spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("module", r"C:\Temp\__pycache__\check.cpython-39.pyc") module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) # Execute the module using exec_module try: spec.loader.exec_module(module) except Exception as e: print(f"An error occurred: {e}")
documents.s: 3. Create a Script (Exec.py) to Execute the .pyc

documents.t: It can be executed from an IDE, batch file, launcher, or the Jupiter ribbon.

Use the python.exe located directly under the Jupiter installation directory to compile .py → .pyc. Standard output is overridden, so print statements do not work after .pyc compilation. In such cases, use JPT.MsgOut(). Example: check_print.py import JPT import Geometry Geometry.Part.Cube() JPT.ViewFitToModel() faces = JPT.GetAllFaces() for face in faces: JPT.SelectionByID(JPT.EntityType.FACE, face.id, True) JPT.MsgOut(f'A cube is created and all the {len(faces)} faces are selected.') Exec.py import importlib.util import sys # Load and execute the .pyc file spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("module", r"C:\Temp\__pycache__\check_print.cpython-39.pyc") module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) # Execute the module using exec_module try: spec.loader.exec_module(module) except AttributeError as e: print(f"Error during module execution: {e}") except Exception as e: print(f"An unexpected error occurred: {e}") The if __name__ == '__main__': block will not be executed. If necessary, explicitly call module.main(). Example: Exec.py try: spec.loader.exec_module(module) module.main() except Exception as e: print(f"An error occurred: {e}") For importing PSJ Command modules, ensure to import each module used in your script. For example, if using a PSJ Command for surface meshing: import Meshing Note that some functions may not work properly when compiled to .pyc.

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to read and write file with PSJ-Utility: Set path of file for reading/writing. Check the existing of file. Read file content with different purpose: line by line directly/ whole file / specific characters. Write content to file with append or write option. Please prepare the text file in local disk to use the code in sample. Administration rights can be an issue when reading/writing file to C:/ drive, be noticed.

# Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Set path of file, it must be an existed file myFile = 'D:/myFile.txt' # Check file exist or not. If not exist, display information at Python API window. import os.path if not os.path.exists(myFile): print("file is not exist!") # Prepare the text file in local disk to use the below code ########## Read file ########## # Read line by line. Display content at Python API window. file = open(myFile, "r") for line in file: print(line) file.close() # Read whole content of file. Display content at Python API window. file = open(myFile, "r") print(file.read()) file.close() # Read first 4 characters of file. Display content at Python API window. file = open(myFile, "r") print(file.read(4)) file.close() ########## Write file ########## # Append 'a' content at the end of file file = open(myFile, "a") file.write("\nAdd new line, write new content") file.close() # Read 'r' whole content of file after appending. Display content at Python API window. file = open(myFile, "r") print(file.read()) file.close() # Write 'w' content to file. Create a new file if file does not exist file = open(myFile, "w") file.write("Existing content of file is deleted. New content is overwritten") file.close() # Read 'r' whole content of file after overwrite. Display content at Python API window. file = open(myFile, "r") print(file.read()) file.close()

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to use Pandas to do calculation with meshed model: Read mesh information of all parts. Get area for each element in all parts. Finally, export the results to MS Excel file using Pandas (each part name in separate sheet).

# Encoding for Japanese # coding: cp932 # Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Make 4 sample models (if you already had a model opened, ignore the below code) Geometry.Part.Cube(ilAxialNodes=[9, 7, 5]) Geometry.Part.Cylinder(dlOrigin=[0.03, 0.0, 0.0], dTopOuterRadius=0.005, dBottomOuterRadius=0.005, dHeight=0.03, iCircularNodes=10, iAxialNodes=300, iPartColor=6409934) Geometry.Part.Sphere(dlOrigin=[0.06, 0.0, 0.0], iLatitudeDivisions=100, iLongitudeDivisions=40, iPartColor=13259210) Geometry.Part.Torus(dlOrigin=[0.12, 0.0, 0.0], iCircumNodes=100, iRingNodes=30, iPartColor=7697908) # Change this location to your folder xlsx_file = "D:/output.xlsx" ############################################################################################# #################################### Start the main code #################################### ############################################################################################# import JPT import pandas as pd import os shell_elem_type = ["ELEMTYPE_TRI3", "ELEMTYPE_QUAD4", "ELEMTYPE_QUAD8", "ELEMTYPE_TRI6"] solid_elem_type = ["ELEMTYPE_HEX8", "ELEMTYPE_HEX20", "ELEMTYPE_PRISM6", "ELEMTYPE_PRISM15", "ELEMTYPE_TET4", "ELEMTYPE_TET10"] shell_elem_area = {} solid_elem = [] count = 0 print("Exporting the shell area for each element of shell parts ...") JPT.DisableOutputMessage() for part in JPT.GetAllParts(): df = pd.DataFrame() elem_id_list = [] elem_area_list = [] check_solid = False for elem in part.elems: if str(elem.type).strip() in shell_elem_type: elem_id_list.append(elem.id) elem_area_list.append(float(JPT.Exec('measure_area_elem([11:{}], 10)'.format(elem.id))) * 1000000) elif str(elem.type).strip() in solid_elem_type: solid_elem.append(part.name) check_solid = True break if check_solid == False: df["Elem ID"] = elem_id_list df["Elem Area (mm2)"] = elem_area_list shell_elem_area.update({part.name: df}) count += 1 JPT.EnableOutputMessage() if count > 0: writer = pd.ExcelWriter(xlsx_file, engine='xlsxwriter') for key in shell_elem_area.keys(): shell_elem_area[key].to_excel(writer, sheet_name = key, index = False) writer.save() writer.close() print("The exportation process is finished!") else: print("Shell parts are not exist on this model")

Load sample model into Jupiter. jupiterPath = JPT.GetAppPathInfo(JPT.PathType.PROGRAM_PATH) samplePath = jupiterPath + '/SampleData/PSJ/PSJ-Utility/JtdbSample/EntityModel.jtdb' FileMenu.LoadJTDB(samplePath) # Fit view of model on display view JPT.ViewFitToModel() # Remove all Load and Boundary Conditions from database JPT.RemoveAllLoadsBCs() # Get list of all 'LOCAL_SETTING' entity in model # Remove local mesh setting by specific name listLocalSetting = JPT.GetAllByType(JPT.DItemType.LOCAL_SETTING) for localSetting in listLocalSetting: if localSetting.name == "MeshParam_1": JPT.RemoveEntitiesByID(JPT.DItemType.LOCAL_SETTING, localSetting.id) # Remove 'BODY' entity / part by id 1 JPT.RemoveEntitiesByID(JPT.DItemType.BODY, 1)

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to register PSJ to Jupiter's ribbon, similarly to built-in functions: Add a PSJ file with icon as a button in a customized ribbon. Create customized ribbon groups of PSJ function with separators.

In the PSJ-Command custom folder (Preferences > Path Setting > PSJ Command), create a new folder as the ribbon name which you want to create. In the created folder, copy (or replace) the created .py file. If you need an icon, you can create an .ico file and copy (or replace) to this ribbon folder. The name of .ico file has to be the same with the name of .py file. If there is no second folder, Ribbon name is used as the Group name and placed at the first item in ribbon. You can further create customized ribbon groups of PSJ function (with separators) using below rule: First folder: Ribbon name (use folder name as Ribbon name, accept white space) Second folder: Group name (use folder name as Group name, accept white space) Third folder: Function name (use Python filename as Function name, accept white space) Functions can be arranged using number prefix, but need to have the same number of characters. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to select or deselect entities on display view: Change selector entity to Part. Select/Deselect entity by Part entity type and ID. Select/Deselect all entities has Part entity type. Change selector entity to Face, select all entities has Face entity type. Deselect all current selected entities. Example of entity types for select method: Part: JPT.SelectMethodType.SELMTD_BODY Face: JPT.SelectMethodType.SELMTD_FACE Edge: JPT.SelectMethodType.SELMTD_EDGE Node: JPT.SelectMethodType.SELMTD_NODE 2D Element: JPT.SelectMethodType.SELMTD_ELEM In this tutorial, Part (Body) and Face entities are used. Other entities can be used as same way.

# Encoding for Japanese # coding: cp932 # Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Create sample model Geometry.Part.Cube() Geometry.Part.Cube(dlOrigin=[0.01, 0.0, 0.0], strName="Cube_2", iPartColor=6409934) # Fit view of model on display view JPT.ViewFitToModel() # Change selector entity to 'Part' JPT.SetSelectMethod(JPT.SelectMethodType.SELMTD_BODY) ########## Select/Deselect entity by entity's type and ID ########## # Select/Deselect 'Part' entity has ID 1 # Select mode: True, Deselect mode: False JPT.SelectionByID(JPT.DItemType.BODY, 1, True) JPT.SelectionByID(JPT.DItemType.BODY, 1, False) ########## Select/Deselect entities by entity's type ########## # Select/Deselect all entities has type: 'Part' # Select mode: True, Deselect mode: False JPT.SelectionByType(JPT.DItemType.BODY, True) JPT.SelectionByType(JPT.DItemType.BODY, False) # Change selector entity to 'Face' # Select all entities has type: 'Face' JPT.SetSelectMethod(JPT.SelectMethodType.SELMTD_FACE) JPT.SelectionByType(JPT.DItemType.FACE, True) # Deselect all current selected entities JPT.ClearAllSelection()

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to use numpy library for: Making a matrix with size nx3 (n is number of nodes) containing nodal locations. Returning the indices of the maximum values along an axis. Sorting the matrix. Calculating mean value in each row.

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to make a simple machine learning model by using only the first feature of the diabetes dataset, in order to illustrate the data points within the two-dimensional plot. The straight line can be seen in the plot, showing how linear regression attempts to draw a straight line that will best minimize the residual sum of squares between the observed responses in the dataset, and the responses predicted by the linear approximation. The coefficients, residual sum of squares and the coefficient of determination are also calculated. Coefficients: [938.23786125] Mean squared error: 2548.07 Coefficient of determination: 0.47 This sample is referenced from scikit-learn website.

# Encoding for Japanese # coding: cp932 import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np from sklearn import datasets, linear_model from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error, r2_score # Load the diabetes dataset diabetes_X, diabetes_y = datasets.load_diabetes(return_X_y=True) # Use only one feature diabetes_X = diabetes_X[:, np.newaxis, 2] # Split the data into training/testing sets diabetes_X_train = diabetes_X[:-20] diabetes_X_test = diabetes_X[-20:] # Split the targets into training/testing sets diabetes_y_train = diabetes_y[:-20] diabetes_y_test = diabetes_y[-20:] # Create linear regression object regr = linear_model.LinearRegression() # Train the model using the training sets regr.fit(diabetes_X_train, diabetes_y_train) # Make predictions using the testing set diabetes_y_pred = regr.predict(diabetes_X_test) # The coefficients print('Coefficients: \n', regr.coef_) # The mean squared error print('Mean squared error: %.2f' % mean_squared_error(diabetes_y_test, diabetes_y_pred)) # The coefficient of determination: 1 is perfect prediction print('Coefficient of determination: %.2f' % r2_score(diabetes_y_test, diabetes_y_pred)) # Plot outputs plt.scatter(diabetes_X_test, diabetes_y_test, color='black') plt.plot(diabetes_X_test, diabetes_y_pred, color='blue', linewidth=3) plt.xticks(()) plt.yticks(()) plt.show()

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to write information of selected faces from Jupiter model to CSV file: Import csv module. Get list of selected faces entity from user selection in Jupiter. Write related information of selected faces to CSV file. Before running the script, you need to prepare the model and select some faces in the model

# Import csv module import csv # Clear the log message in Python API window JPT.ClearLog() # Get list of selected faces entity from user selection in Jupiter listFaces = JPT.GetSelectedFaces() # Write related information of selected faces to CSV file with open(r"D:/facelist.csv", "w", newline="") as file: writer = csv.writer(file) writer.writerow(["No.", "ID", "Entity", "Part", "Information", "X", "Y", "Z"]) i = 0 for face in listFaces: i = i + 1 listPart = JPT.GetEntitiesByAssociation(JPT.DItemType.FACE, JPT.AssociateType.AS_BODY, face.id) writer.writerow([i, str(face.id), "Face", listPart[0].name]) print("Finished")
